quote_a: anything hostile that crosses the boundary gets read and redirected down a channel she chose while writing it
quote_b: it reads trajectory rather than intent
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Archivium Locus.md
why: The Effect selects on hostility; the Mechanism is oscillator coupling, which selects on trajectory and cannot tell a hostile line from a friendly one. The page's own Weakness says so. Either the lattice redirects every fast-moving thing that enters, including allies and thrown ropes, or something not in the Mechanism is doing the sorting.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the lattice redirects any coupled trajectory, friend or foe.
options.changes: Makes the working a hazard to her own side and gives a real tactical cost to a 60 m field; forces the Design Chain's Effect line to be rewritten.

options.option: Add a recognition layer to the Mechanism, naming the Wellspring or Sub-Stat that performs it.
options.changes: Adds a second law to the working, a second gate to check in Part Seven, and probably a second cost; the Judicium precedent exists on Bastion Imperium.

options.option: Keep both and rule that the pre-written channels encode friendly vectors, so allies are redirected harmlessly.
options.changes: No new law; converts 'hostile' into 'not pre-authorised' and makes the channel list a piece of pre-battle planning a player can attack.

options.option: Rule that the lattice reads trajectory only and delete 'hostile' from the Effect.
options.changes: Smallest change; the Weakness line becomes the whole truth and the tunnel counter gets stronger.

quote_a: whichever of an event's already-possible outcomes she prefers becomes the one that happens; nothing new is conjured, only chosen
quote_b: Fractura's refraction law is used to hold an event's several physically possible outcome-paths open at once
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Auric Parallax Veil.md
why: The Effect claims pure selection with nothing added. The Mechanism first manufactures a state that was not there — several paths held open at once — and only then selects. Holding open is an act with a cost, and the page bills nothing for it. Related to the physics fault at SA-PHYS-PARALLAX-SUPERPOSITION-VS-SELECTION but distinct: this is the page contradicting itself, not the page contradicting physics.

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism as reweighting an existing distribution, with no paths held open.
options.changes: Aligns Mechanism with Effect and with the physics reading that closes; removes the superposition language entirely.

options.option: Keep the holding-open and add its cost to the Effect and the ledger.
options.changes: Gives the Veil a second, larger price and a new failure mode when the holding lapses; the overload counter then follows naturally.

options.option: Split into two workings: one that holds branches open, one that selects.
options.changes: Two Codex entries, two Stage floors, and a combination a player can interrupt between halves.

options.option: Rule that 'held open' is the in-world school's language for reweighting, not a mechanic.
options.changes: Nothing changes mechanically; the phrase moves into the lens in section 2 and the Mechanism is restated in selection terms.

quote_a: any force below the Stage's own threshold loses power against him
quote_b: force arriving under the Stage's threshold is read, weighed, and found wanting before it is allowed to register at all
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Bastion Imperium.md
why: The Coagula half of the Mechanism is a real load path: man and ground gathered into one structure, so momentum goes into a much larger mass. The Judicium half is a verdict, and a verdict is not a mechanism — 'found wanting before it is allowed to register' does not say where the joules go. Under Addendum 2 the effect must be the law running, and here the threshold behaviour has no law under it.

options.option: Drop the Judicium verdict language and let the load path do all the work: force below the threshold is absorbed by the combined mass of man and ground.
options.changes: Explains the threshold as a mass ratio, makes it computable, and ties the 10 m radius to how much ground is gathered; Judicium becomes flavour or leaves the working.

options.option: Keep Judicium and state what it does with the energy — shunt it into the ground, re-radiate it, or convert it.
options.changes: Needs a named sink and a bleed figure at his η; may breach the Aetheric Density question at SA-GAP-AETHER-AS-SINK.

options.option: Recast the threshold as a stress limit rather than a filter: below it the structure does not yield, above it it does.
options.changes: Removes the need for any selection at all, matches real structural behaviour, and keeps the S-band numbers as a yield stress.

options.option: Rule the verdict is genuine Judicium law and log a standing exception to the Index's 'a glyph cannot attack a law'.
options.changes: Large: would license verdict-as-mechanism across every Judicium working in the batch, including Crimson Dirge.

quote_a: a rotating crystalline shard built from ten Wellspring laws held in simultaneous contradiction
quote_b: Ten Wellspring laws are phase-locked onto one lattice through Orrenthal's resonance as the reference frequency, the way an interferometer holds several light paths in one stable fringe pattern
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Celestial Decree Aeon-Shard Mandate.md
why: Contradiction and phase-lock are opposites. A stable fringe pattern is ten paths in agreement; contradiction is what an interferometer cannot hold. The Effect's drama and the Mechanism's physics are pulling in opposite directions, and which one is true decides whether the shard is beaten by breaking the reference tone or by resolving the contradiction.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect as ten laws held in coherence, not contradiction.
options.changes: Mechanism becomes the whole account; the counter is the reference frequency, and a Silence beats the shard outright.

options.option: Keep contradiction and replace the interferometer with a mechanism that can hold incompatibles.
options.changes: Needs a new law the system does not currently supply; would probably require a ruling on whether anything below Archonic can hold a contradiction.

options.option: Rule that the contradiction is between the laws' *domains* while their phases agree.
options.changes: Reconciles both lines at the cost of a definition; the lens in section 2 already frames this as the Cusa question.

options.option: Reduce the count from ten to the number an interferometer reading actually needs.
options.changes: Smaller, cheaper working; loses the 'ten Wellsprings' signature that the Harmonics Breadth gate is built around.

quote_a: wards, illusions and layered constructs break all at once rather than one layer at a time
quote_b: a target holding several contradictory frequencies at once denies the Shear a single clean frequency to find and cut
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Celestial Harmonic Shear.md
why: The Mechanism is resonant decoupling at one characteristic frequency. A layered construct has several distinct modes, so one cut at one frequency cannot fail all of them simultaneously — and the page's own Counter says frequency multiplicity defeats the Shear. The Effect therefore claims the exact behaviour the Counter says is impossible.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect: the Shear cuts the layer whose frequency it locked, and the rest hold.
options.changes: Makes the working single-mode, consistent with its Counter; layered wards become a real defence and the technique needs repeat casts it cannot afford.

options.option: Keep simultaneous failure and explain it as a shared load-bearing mode across the layers.
options.changes: Requires that layered constructs have one common mode, which then becomes a general rule about Runecraft layering and a new thing for players to attack.

options.option: Rule that the Shear sweeps a band rather than a line, cutting every mode inside it.
options.changes: Raises cost and yield, needs a band width in the ledger, and weakens the multiplicity counter without removing it.

options.option: Split the difference: all layers whose frequencies fall within the locked mode's linewidth fail together.
options.changes: Adds one derivable number (linewidth, and therefore Q) and keeps both lines partly true.

quote_a: a hostile working that reaches the corona is stripped of its lethal vector and shed as harmless light
quote_b: a reflective boundary shaped by Aurevane's own law of illumination redirects incoming Aether along the corona's surface rather than letting it strike home, and the fraction of that redirected energy that escapes outward is what reads as light
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Corona Lunaris.md
why: Reflection conserves energy; it does not render it harmless. The Mechanism redirects, and the page's own threshold is a cumulative 46 GJ — so up to 46 GJ has to leave as light, which at that scale is not harmless to eyes, skin or anything nearby. 'Harmless' is an Effect the Mechanism does not produce. Distinct from SA-PHYS-CORONA-HARMLESS-LIGHT, which asks where the joules go; this asks which of the page's own two sentences is canon.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect: the corona redirects rather than neutralises, and the shed light is itself dangerous at high loads.
options.changes: Adds a real area hazard to a defensive working, makes allies inside the half-sphere a consideration, and turns brightness into a warning rather than a reassurance.

options.option: Keep 'harmless' and name where the energy actually goes — into the Crown, into the ground, into the Aether stratum.
options.changes: Needs a sink and a capacity; if the Crown is the sink, Crown Fatigue becomes quantifiable in joules.

options.option: Lower the threshold so the light shed is never at a harmful scale.
options.changes: Makes the corona a much weaker save, consistent with Stage V, and probably drops it below usefulness against S-Grade attacks.

options.option: Rule the conversion is genuinely lossy and most of the energy is destroyed rather than redirected.
options.changes: Breaks conservation deliberately and needs a standing ruling; would apply to every Aurevane working.

quote_a: Banks incoming kinetic, thermal, emotional, and Aetheric force as stored equilibrium, then discharges it as one decisive corrective act while the remainder bleeds off as harmless cold
quote_b: Force is caught and held as potential rather than expressed, the way a compressed spring stores work rather than losing it
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Cryost Ascendant.md
why: The Effect gives the same joules two incompatible fates: banked for discharge, and bled off as cold. The Mechanism supplies only the first. And a spring that keeps its work does not radiate — the cold cannot be the surplus leaving if the surplus is being kept. Related to SA-PHYS-CRYOST-COLD-DIRECTION, which asks why arrested energy shows as cold at all; this asks whether the working keeps the energy or sheds it.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect: everything caught is banked, and the cold is the signature of the bank rather than a bleed.
options.changes: Removes the 'harmless cold' escape valve, so the bank must always be discharged or set into him; strengthens the overbanking cost.

options.option: Keep the bleed and give it a fraction: x per cent banked at his η, the rest radiated.
options.changes: Makes the ledger computable from η and bounds the discharge; needs one number Isaac sets.

options.option: Rule the cold is the bleed and the bank is the intended output, i.e. ordinary 1 − η bleed wearing a Vohrin coat.
options.changes: No new mechanic at all: the cold becomes the batch's standard heat/sound/structural bleed, and SA-PHYS-CRYOST-COLD-DIRECTION collapses into it.

options.option: Split the working: one mode banks, one mode radiates, and it cannot do both.
options.changes: Adds a stance choice the practitioner must declare, which is a tell and a limit at once.

quote_a: local physics inside a one-kilometre radius run on rewritten equations for the duration
quote_b: the local coupling constants that ordinarily fix how strongly a given law applies at Francis's own scale are pushed, for the duration, toward the values those same laws take at a deeper, Archon-adjacent scale
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Dirge Ascension.md
why: Moving a coupling constant is staying inside the same equation with a different number in it. Rewriting the equations is a different and much larger claim. The distinction is not cosmetic: under the Mechanism every law still holds and only its strength changes, which is exactly what the Master Glyph Index permits a boundary condition to do; under the Effect the laws themselves are replaced, which the Index says cannot be done.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the same laws, at different strengths, for 45 seconds.
options.changes: Keeps the working inside the Index's rule, makes it calculable from the couplings moved, and tells a defender which laws to rely on.

options.option: Keep 'rewritten equations' and log a standing exception to the Index for proto-Archonic states.
options.changes: Large: creates a class of workings that genuinely replace laws, with Crimson Dirge as the other candidate.

options.option: Name which couplings move and by how much.
options.changes: Turns the whole working into a derivable table and gives players something to look up and exploit; the hardest option and the most rewarding.

options.option: Rule that at Zenith the distinction is not assessable, per Part Four's own caution on conventional metrics.
options.changes: Nothing changes; the ambiguity becomes canon and SA-NUM-ZENITH-CONVENTIONAL-METRICS absorbs it.

quote_a: A downward blade strike gains metaphysical mass in proportion to the hesitation Drakvor reads in his target
quote_b: Here it reads the target's own hesitation and feeds that reading into the strike's weight
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Edict Strike.md
why: A reading is information. Information is not a source of mass or momentum, and the Mechanism supplies no store the extra weight is drawn from — Coagula is said to gather 'that borrowed weight', but nothing says whose it was. The doubling is an Effect with no law under it.

options.option: Name the source: the doubled weight is drawn from the ambient Aether, with the target's hesitation as the boundary condition that authorises the draw.
options.changes: Puts the joules where Two Sets of Books puts them, makes the cost a draw rather than free, and gives the working a Field fault in thin ground.

options.option: Recast the effect as a defence penalty rather than an attack bonus: the hesitant target resists worse, so the same blow does more.
options.changes: No new energy needed at all — the cleanest fix, and it moves the working from Ardency to a Gnosis-versus-Resilience contest.

options.option: Make the doubling a Coagula gathering of the target's own committed Essence, turned against them.
options.changes: Explains the source and creates a counter: spend nothing and there is nothing to gather.

options.option: Drop the doubling and let the reading grant accuracy or timing instead of weight.
options.changes: Keeps the working in band (see SA-NUM-EDICT-SS-PUSH) and removes the physics problem entirely.

quote_a: A lethal blow becomes a disarm; a Wellspring is barred from being invoked to shed blood; the Edict, not Serenyra, is what refuses
quote_b: Judicium's law of discernment and consequence is what lets the Edict recognize the named action when it happens; Aurevane carries the enforcement evenly across the whole dome
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Edictum Resonantiae.md
why: The Mechanism explains how the Edict notices a banned action and how far the noticing reaches. It never says what converts the lethal blow into a disarm. Recognition plus carriage is a sensor and a wire; the actuator is missing, and the Effect is entirely actuator.

options.option: Name the enforcing law: a third Wellspring or a stated Coagula/Transference redirection that performs the rerouting.
options.changes: Adds one Wellspring and one gate to check; makes the Edict's strength a function of that law rather than of her standing.

options.option: Rule that the Edict conditions the Threshold rather than the action — an unlawful working is never authorised, so it does not happen.
options.changes: Elegant and system-native: moves the whole working into authorisation, which the Counterplay register already treats as a real attack surface. Physical blows would then be untouched, shrinking the Effect.

options.option: Keep the rerouting and price it: every conversion costs her, so the dome has a budget.
options.changes: Turns a 200 m dome into a resource and gives attackers a way to exhaust it by committing cheap banned actions.

options.option: Reduce the Effect to suppression only — the action fails, nothing is rerouted.
options.changes: Smallest change; 'a lethal blow becomes a disarm' leaves the page and recognition-plus-refusal is enough.

quote_a: having genuinely crossed the intervening distance rather than having erased and remade themselves at the far end
quote_b: The caster's body attenuates and reconstitutes at the far mass with no intervening state anyone watching can resolve
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Fluxus Intervallum.md
why: The page insists three times that the crossing is real traversal and not a disappearance and a remaking, and then its Target Response describes attenuation and reconstitution — which is the disappearance and the remaking. Which one is true decides whether an obstruction on the line stops it, and the obstruction is the page's own cheapest counter.

options.option: Rewrite the Target Response as a real crossing too fast to resolve.
options.changes: Consistent with the Effect and with the line-obstruction counter; forces the speed question at SA-NUM-FLUXUS-INSTANT-VS-B-SPEED to be answered rather than avoided.

options.option: Accept attenuation and reconstitution, and rewrite the Effect and the obstruction counter accordingly.
options.changes: The line stops mattering, so the page loses its best counter and needs a new one; also changes what Transference is for.

options.option: Rule that 'attenuates' describes what an observer sees of a real crossing, not what happens.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the phrase is marked as an observer report and the Mechanism stands.

options.option: Make it a real crossing that is briefly non-solid, so obstructions matter but soft cover does not.
options.changes: Adds a middle case with a stated threshold, and gives players a reason to care what the obstruction is made of.

quote_a: Serenyra sees its structure exposed as suspended, legible form, and can unravel it, alter it, or simply learn from it
quote_b: Judicium's discernment law reads the working the way a Thaumic Harmonist reads a spell's tonal composition: compatible components register as consonance, structural flaws register as dissonance she can locate precisely
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Lumen Dissecans.md
why: The Mechanism is entirely diagnostic — a read, carried outward as visible light by Aurevane. Nothing in it unravels or alters anything. Unravelling a working is a second operation with its own law, its own cost and its own gate, and the page bills only for the beam.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect: the beam exposes and holds open, and unravelling or altering requires a separate working performed in the window.
options.changes: The cleanest fix and the most playable: the dissection becomes a setup, the window becomes precious, and the follow-up is its own cast with its own tell.

options.option: Name the law that unravels, and price it separately in the ledger.
options.changes: Adds a Wellspring and a gate; the 22 AU/s share then covers only the read.

options.option: Rule that a working held open at its own frequencies comes apart under the drive itself, so unravelling is the read continued.
options.changes: Physically defensible (driven past its damping) and needs no new law — but it means the beam always risks destroying what she wanted to archive.

options.option: Reduce the Effect to reading and archiving only.
options.changes: Smallest change; removes an offensive use and makes the technique purely analytic, which matches the Wellspring.

quote_a: overlays a chosen false environment across up to 120 m, so that anyone inside sees, hears and feels a world she has selected rather than the one that is actually there
quote_b: Oneirion's conceptual-form law writes a false perceptual state directly onto the target's sensory processing rather than onto the environment itself
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Liminal Palace of False Dawn.md
why: A 120 m overlay is a thing in a place; a write onto sensory processing is a thing in a head. The page's own Trigger makes it worse by adding a doorway that must be 'stepped through or gestured through'. Whether the Palace is a region or a per-mind state decides who is affected: someone who never crossed the threshold, someone who arrives later, someone watching from outside with a spyglass.

options.option: Rule it is per-mind, with 120 m as the range within which she can write to a mind.
options.changes: The doorway becomes a focus rather than a boundary; late arrivals are affected on entry into range, and a distant observer is not. Matches the Mechanism.

options.option: Rule it is a genuine field, and rewrite the Mechanism to write onto the space.
options.changes: Contradicts 'never touches physical reality' and would need a new law; but it makes the doorway meaningful and the working easier to run at a table.

options.option: Keep both: a field that writes to every mind inside it, with the doorway as the enrolment condition.
options.changes: Needs one ruling on what happens to someone who enters without passing the door — which is exactly the kind of question the counter should turn on.

options.option: Shrink the Effect to those who cross the threshold, whatever the radius.
options.changes: Makes the doorway the whole working, gives a hard and obvious counter (do not go in), and keeps the Mechanism untouched.

quote_a: The heartbeat goes wrong while the graft holds. Temporary. It has never once stopped him.
quote_b: It costs something that hurts. EU at a rate that reaches Starvation in a real fight, Harmonics, Coherence, the body, or a vow.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: The page states its cost and then withdraws it in the next clause. A cost that has never once mattered is not a cost that hurts. What actually limits the working is the thinning of each talon's residue on reuse, which the page files under Weakness rather than Cost and never quantifies.

options.option: Promote the residue thinning to the Cost and give it a rate — so many draws per talon.
options.changes: Makes his trophy belt a countable resource, rewards players who track what he has used, and needs one number.

options.option: Give the arrhythmia a real consequence: a stat penalty, a duration cap, or a risk of Structural fault on repeat grafts.
options.changes: Keeps the stated cost and makes it bite; needs a threshold Isaac sets.

options.option: Bill the graft in EU as a fraction of reserve, as Bloodbind Surge does.
options.changes: The only option that produces a Starvation margin, and it would make the two Draven buff techniques price-comparable.

options.option: Accept it as a cheap Stage VI utility and rely on the environmental and seal counters instead.
options.changes: No change; records that the fairness of this page rests entirely on its limits and not on its price.

quote_a: pushing his own A-Grade Ardency baseline (20–100 GN peak, 46 GJ–4 TJ yield, per the FOW Physical Benchmarks table) toward the top of that band or briefly past it
quote_b: Stage VI · Glory · Max Grade A · Sub-Stat ceiling 400
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Stage VI's Max Grade is A with a ceiling of 400 and, unlike Stages V, VII and IX, no documented instability zone above it. The system therefore provides no rule under which a Stage VI practitioner reads above A, even briefly, so 'or briefly past it' is out of band rather than generously in it. Its numbers-in-band check fails.

options.option: Delete 'or briefly past it' and cap the surge at the top of A.
options.changes: Smallest change; the tripling then has to fit inside the A band, which it does if the baseline is read from the band's floor.

options.option: Keep the overshoot and route it through Ardency Overchannel's documented Overflow and Backlash risks.
options.changes: Uses a rule that already exists in Part Seven and adds a real chance of hurting himself; needs a stated risk threshold.

options.option: Give Stage VI an instability zone, as Stages V, VII and IX have.
options.changes: A system-level change affecting every Stage VI character, not just Draven.

options.option: Reduce the multiplier from triple to whatever keeps him inside A from his stated baseline.
options.changes: Purely numeric, checkable by a reader, and preserves the ten-second/70-per-cent economy untouched.

quote_a: A fellow Stage XII being can force a contradictory harmonic state through direct law interference; pure Verdantia resists the destructive vectors; Hypnather constructs can invert the dream-logic layer; a sufficiently massive Petralon entity can absorb the collapse beam
quote_b: Something beats it. At least one of the four Counterplay routes … works, and the write-up names which. … No answer to everything, and no immunity to all four routes.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Every counter the page names requires a peer, a Titan-scale mass, or a Wellspring alignment. Nothing is offered to a party below Stage XII, which fails the fairness rule directly. Two routes are in fact open and the page does not acknowledge either: Silence takes away the Orrenthal reference frequency the lattice locks to, and the woman raising her hand is a person who can be shot.

options.option: Name Silence, or the loss of the reference tone, as a counter on the page.
options.changes: Costs nothing and makes the working beatable by an administrative decision, which the Counterplay register says is how most serious actions begin.

options.option: Name the contradiction clause as an exploitable counter: force a demand for destruction and restoration at once.
options.changes: Turns a stated limit into a stated counter; requires no new mechanic.

options.option: Add an ordinary-means route — the shard's autonomy is finite and she is a body at the centre.
options.changes: Restores 'break the body' and makes the 'short intervals' of autonomy a number worth stating.

options.option: Accept peer-only counters and log the working as a set-piece that is not meant to be beaten in a fight.
options.changes: Explicit and honest; means it should never be pointed at a party, which is a Front-level decision rather than a technique one.

quote_a: Sustained use exhausts the harmonics that keep her ten Wellsprings integrated, risking a partial Temperance shear or a flattening of her own affect; prolonged projection risks her own mind bleeding into the shard's judgment-logic
quote_b: Below ten percent EU a practitioner suffers Essence Starvation: reduced stat expression, Shell degradation, Trait flickering.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The costs are the right kind — a Temperance shear is catastrophic and identity loss is permanent — but both are gated on the words 'sustained' and 'prolonged' with no duration, no fraction of reserve and no EU figure. Nothing in a single engagement can be made to fall due. Compare Bloodbind Surge, where 70 per cent of reserve per minute makes the cost a countdown a player can run.

options.option: State the cost as a fraction of reserve per unit time, as Bloodbind Surge does.
options.changes: Produces a Starvation margin and makes the shard a clock; the single most useful change for play.

options.option: Define 'sustained' and 'prolonged' as stated numbers of exchanges.
options.changes: Cheap; turns both costs into thresholds a player can count toward.

options.option: Charge per mode switch rather than per unit time.
options.changes: Makes versatility the expensive part, which fits a working whose selling point is that it does three things.

options.option: Give the shard a hard duration after which it lapses regardless.
options.changes: Bounds the encounter without pricing anything, and creates the survivable-window counter Dirge Ascension already has.

quote_a: Aeldoris takes on a brief sensory overlay of his own field's contradictions (Double Vision), and the field leaves a residue that bleeds into the ground for a time after the fight ends (Dream Residue)
quote_b: It costs something that hurts.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Neither cost degrades his output, neither is priced in EU or as a fraction of reserve, neither can reach Starvation, and Dream Residue is paid by the ground rather than by him. Against a 40 m field that spoils aim, timing and every other participant's reading of their own cost, that is not a price.

options.option: Bill the claim in EU per second of hold, as Maw of Crystalline Stasis is billed.
options.changes: Gives a Starvation margin and a reason he cannot hold it all fight; needs one rate.

options.option: Make Double Vision bite: a stated penalty to his own accuracy or timing while the field stands.
options.changes: Elegant — the field's own effect applied to its author — and needs no new number, only a stated penalty.

options.option: Charge Coherence or Harmonics for holding two contradictory accounts of a room open.
options.changes: Uses costs the system already has and ties the price to what makes the working unusual.

options.option: Make Dream Residue a liability he carries rather than one the ground carries — a mark that can be read and followed.
options.changes: Converts a cosmetic aftermath into an investigative handle and a Front consequence, at no mechanical cost.

quote_a: An Archonic mandate outranks the borrowed authority of the form outright. A Nihiloth-mediated null field (Talos-class) can suppress the transformation's output, though a full null against an EX-Grade spike is not guaranteed.
quote_b: Something beats it. At least one of the four Counterplay routes … works, and the write-up names which.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Both named counters sit at or above his own register, and the page concedes the second is not assured. No route is named for anyone below that tier, even though two exist and are findable: the duration is a stated, counted 45 seconds ending in paradox recoil, and the working overstates a Fate-Path warrant it does not hold, which the Counterplay register says can be billed by forcing an early Seal.

options.option: Name the 45-second window and the recoil as a counter on the page.
options.changes: Costs nothing, is already true, and converts the working from unanswerable into survivable — the register's 'waiting for the cost' warning does not apply because the window is printed.

options.option: Name the unmet Fate gate as an attack surface: a third party who forces an early close bills him the difference.
options.changes: Uses 'Force the Seal early' verbatim from the register and rewards a player who read Part Seven.

options.option: Add a field-denial route below Archonic — saturated cold, a shielded interior, thermal equilibrium against the Caloria half.
options.changes: Gives ordinary preparation a purchase on a Zenith working without touching its output.

options.option: Accept it as unanswerable at sub-peer level and restrict it to set-piece use.
options.changes: Honest; makes its appearance a Front decision rather than a combat option.

quote_a: A held verdict, reached before the strike lands. … A strike thrown without that verdict already formed does not carry the working.
quote_b: It has a tell. A careful opponent can read it coming.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: The trigger is an internal state with no stated outward sign, and the discharge is instant at 150 m with no sustain phase. From outside, a Final Mercy and an ordinary strike from the same man are indistinguishable until one of them has already resolved. The only diagnostic the page offers — emotional silence and absent residue — arrives after the target is gone.

options.option: Give the verdict an outward form: a spoken sentence, a raised seal, a visible change in the blade or the light.
options.changes: Costs nothing mechanically and makes the technique readable, which is what the challenge rule asks for.

options.option: Make the verdict take time — a held beat between judgment and strike that an opponent can act inside.
options.changes: Creates a real interrupt window and a reason to fight at range; the strongest option for play.

options.option: Rule that Judicium's verdict is legible to anyone with the Wellspring or the training to read it.
options.changes: Makes the counter knowledge-gated rather than universal, and rewards a player who brought the right specialist.

options.option: Accept no tell, and compensate by making the architectural defences more widely available.
options.changes: Shifts fairness entirely onto preparation; means a party without an identity anchor has no play at all.

quote_a: Mild paradox fatigue and Aether recoil after each summoning, worse the more constructs are standing at once.
quote_b: It costs something that hurts.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Three autonomous law-enforcing constructs across a two-kilometre field for twenty-five seconds, priced by the page's own adjective as mild. At the same Stage, Dirge Ascension bills one per cent of Soul Crystal mass per use and Final Mercy four per cent of memory. There is no EU figure, no fraction of reserve, no Starvation margin, and no point at which a fourth summoning is unaffordable rather than merely impossible.

options.option: Price the summoning in EU per construct per second, so three constructs is three times a stated rate.
options.changes: Makes the ceiling of three an economic choice as well as an architectural one and produces a Starvation margin.

options.option: Charge per construct in Crystal or Coherence terms, matching his other Zenith techniques.
options.changes: Brings the page into line with Dirge Ascension and Final Mercy and makes repeated use a campaign decision.

options.option: Make the recoil scale steeply — quadratically with constructs, as the page's own soliton reasoning implies (N-soliton power goes as N²).
options.changes: Derivable from the mechanism the page already states, so it needs no new rule, only the arithmetic.

options.option: Shorten the duration or the radius until 'mild' is a defensible price.
options.changes: Purely numeric; two kilometres is the largest field in the batch and the least justified by its cost.

quote_a: Opening the blood channel lets the stored print act on his own Aether Shell the way a residue triggers a reaction it does not itself supply
quote_b: The honest answer is that a working's energy budget balances at the Aether stratum and not at the Essence one. The practitioner does not supply the joules.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: The page is explicit that the talon is a catalyst and supplies no power, and equally explicit that the cost is cardiac. So the power for flight, a sonic roar or a burrow reflex comes from neither the talon nor, on the page's own account, the heart. It closes if the working is read as drawing on the ambient field, with the cardiac cost as a Structural fault rather than a fuel bill — but the page never says it draws on the field.

options.option: State that the graft draws on ambient Aether, with the talon's print as the boundary condition.
options.changes: Closes the budget the way Two Sets of Books requires, and gives the working a Field fault in thin or suppressed ground.

options.option: Bill the power to Draven's own reserve in EU and make the cardiac cost the symptom of that draw.
options.changes: Simpler to run, but needs an EU figure and makes the working much more expensive than the page implies.

options.option: Rule that the borrowed trait is expressed at his existing output rather than added to it — he reallocates rather than gains.
options.changes: Needs no new energy at all and matches the page's own cap at his Stage VI ceiling.

options.option: Leave the source unstated and treat the cardiac instability as the whole account.
options.changes: Records the gap as canon; the account keeps the Structural fault and says the budget does not close.

quote_a: Fractura's refraction law is used to hold an event's several physically possible outcome-paths open at once, the way a double-slit interference pattern holds more than one path until something forces a result
quote_b: it cannot originate an outcome that was never a possible branch to begin with
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Auric Parallax Veil.md
why: Two readings are available. Reading A maintains a genuine superposition over macroscopic outcomes, which needs isolation no battlefield provides and no stated cost. Reading B biases an existing probability distribution — a crack initiation site, a turbulent transition, a misfire — which is physically ordinary and needs nothing held open. Reading B closes and Reading A does not. The page's Effect and Limit describe B; its Mechanism describes A.

options.option: Adopt Reading B and rewrite the Mechanism as reweighting a real distribution.
options.changes: Everything closes, the working gets cheaper and more defensible, and the Veil becomes useless against events with no genuine variance — a real and findable limit.

options.option: Adopt Reading A and state what maintains coherence, and what it costs.
options.changes: Needs a new mechanic and a large cost; would make the Veil the most expensive working in the batch.

options.option: Rule the Veil works only on outcomes that are already stochastic, and say so on the page.
options.changes: Formalises Reading B as a limit rather than a mechanism, which is the most playable form.

options.option: Keep both readings as competing in-world accounts under the Four Theories.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the disagreement becomes a school dispute, which the lens in section 2 already sets up.

quote_a: the fraction of that redirected energy that escapes outward is what reads as light. The harder the corona is hit, the brighter it burns.
quote_b: until it has converted a running total of hostile energy and shatters. That threshold is set at 46 GJ
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Corona Lunaris.md
why: Up to 46 GJ is converted and shed as light over at most two turns. Radiated as light that is a flash orders of magnitude beyond anything survivable to look at, and a substantial thermal load on everything nearby. The stratal account says harmless; the physical account cannot. Either the light is dangerous, or most of the energy goes somewhere the page does not name.

options.option: Make the shed light a real hazard scaled to what was absorbed — blinding, then burning.
options.changes: Turns a pure save into a trade-off, gives allies inside the half-sphere something to worry about, and makes the Crown's brightness a warning.

options.option: Name a sink other than radiation: the Crown, the ground, or the Aether stratum.
options.changes: Needs a capacity figure and probably ties into SA-GAP-AETHER-AS-SINK.

options.option: Lower the 46 GJ threshold until the radiated flash is survivable.
options.changes: Makes the corona a much smaller save, appropriate to Stage V, and is purely numeric.

options.option: Rule the conversion destroys rather than redirects most of the energy.
options.changes: A deliberate exception to conservation, applying to all Aurevane workings; needs a standing ruling.

quote_a: The cold the field radiates is the literal thermodynamic signature of arrested kinetic and thermal energy sitting unspent.
quote_b: At Stage IX, S-Grade, the Bloom's held force sits in the 0.5-2 TN, 4.184-24.3 TJ band
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Cryost Ascendant.md
why: Arresting motion releases energy; it does not absorb it. Held as elastic strain, 4.184 TJ needs about 1.67×10⁶ m³ of spring steel at its elastic limit against a field of roughly 2.44×10⁴ m³ — short by about 68 times. Retained as heat the same energy would put the field at order 10⁵ K. Either way the signature of a successful bank is hot, not cold, and the page says cold.

options.option: Rule the cold is the bleed (1 − η) and the bank is elsewhere, in the Aether stratum.
options.changes: Needs no new physics and folds this into the batch's standard bleed; raises the sink question at SA-GAP-AETHER-AS-SINK.

options.option: Reduce the banked energy to what a field that size can plausibly hold and drop the S-Grade band.
options.changes: Makes the working much smaller and entirely consistent; the most conservative fix.

options.option: State that the bank is held at the Essence stratum, not as physical strain, and that cold is what that costs the room.
options.changes: Keeps the numbers and moves the storage off the physical books, which Two Sets of Books explicitly permits.

options.option: Invert the framing: the field cools by taking energy out, and the discharge is that energy returned — so it is a heat engine, not a spring.
options.changes: Explains the cold directly, but then thermal and kinetic vectors are banked by different means and emotional ones need their own account.

quote_a: on the order of 1 PN peak force and roughly 400 TJ yield along the line
quote_b: severing that mode rather than the material itself is the same principle a shattered wineglass or a delaminated composite demonstrates
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Celestial Harmonic Shear.md
why: Resonant decoupling is cheap by design: it works because a small, correctly tuned input accumulates against low damping, which is why a voice can break a glass. Quoting a 400 TJ yield for it describes a brute-force cut and abandons the mechanism that made the working interesting. The stated energy and the stated principle are accounts of two different techniques.

options.option: Drop the force and yield figures and price the Shear by precision and integration time instead.
options.changes: Restores the mechanism, makes the working cheap and surgical, and makes the frequency-multiplicity counter decisive.

options.option: Keep the yield and rewrite the Mechanism as a brute cut.
options.changes: Loses the resonance reading, and with it the page's own Limit about things outside harmonic physics.

options.option: State the yield as what the *target* releases when it fails, not what the Shear delivers.
options.changes: Reconciles both lines at a stroke: the Shear is small, the failure is large, and the number describes the wreckage.

options.option: Give the working a stated gain and Q so the input energy is derivable from the target's own stored energy.
options.changes: The hardest and most rewarding: makes every cut calculable and rewards a player who reads the target's construction.

quote_a: on the order of 1 PN peak force and roughly 400 TJ yield
quote_b: drive any oscillating system hard enough, at its own natural frequency, and amplitude climbs without bound until something in the structure gives
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Harmonic Null-Ascension.md
why: Same fault as its twin, Celestial Harmonic Shear. Resonant forcing past damping is cheap because the energy accumulates in the target over many cycles; the driver supplies a small fraction of the failure energy. A 400 TJ input describes something that did not need resonance at all. The page's own 'the climb begins below the range anything but the Essence layer can register' argues for a small input.

options.option: Price the working by drive time and coupling rather than by delivered yield.
options.changes: Consistent with the mechanism, makes damping the decisive counter, and explains why a few breaths is the limit.

options.option: Report the 400 TJ as the target's own stored energy released at failure.
options.changes: Reconciles both lines and makes the number a consequence rather than an expenditure.

options.option: Keep the yield and drop the resonance reading.
options.changes: Loses the immunity clause for things outside harmonic physics, which is one of the page's best limits.

options.option: State a Q and a drive fraction so the input is derivable.
options.changes: Makes both this page and Celestial Harmonic Shear calculable from one rule, and settles SA-CROSS-SHEAR-NULLASCENSION-TWINS at the same time.

quote_a: Removing or overwhelming a target's senses cuts through the overlay entirely
quote_b: Oneirion's conceptual-form law writes a false perceptual state directly onto the target's sensory processing rather than onto the environment itself, comparable to a forced synesthetic misattribution
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Liminal Palace of False Dawn.md
why: The two halves of the page's own first counter behave oppositely under its own mechanism. Overwhelming the senses raises the precision of the real input, the percept follows it, and the overlay breaks — correct. Removing the senses drives real input to nothing, and a percept with no input is the imposed state alone, so sensory deprivation should make the overlay total rather than penetrable.

options.option: Delete 'removing' and keep 'overwhelming'.
options.changes: Smallest change, consistent with the mechanism, and it makes flooding the senses the canonical counter — loud, cheap and findable.

options.option: Keep both and rule that a mind with no input rejects an unanchored overlay as unreal.
options.changes: Needs a stated reason; would make blindfolding a general counter to every Limina perception working.

options.option: Invert it deliberately: sensory deprivation makes the Palace absolute, and say so on the page.
options.changes: Turns a counter into a trap and rewards players who read the mechanism rather than the counter line — very much in the spirit of the challenge.

options.option: Distinguish by sense: removing sight helps, removing all input does not.
options.changes: Adds a usable rule of thumb at the cost of one more thing to remember.

quote_a: The baseline strike sits at Stage VIII's S-Grade ceiling, 0.5 to 2 TN peak force
quote_b: A downward blade strike
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Edict Strike.md
why: Taking a blade's contact footprint at about 1×10⁻⁷ m², delivering 5×10¹¹ N through it is a contact stress near 5×10¹⁸ Pa. Diamond fails in compression near 1.1×10¹¹ Pa, so the requirement is some 4.5×10⁷ times what any material can carry, and even against diamond 0.5 TN would need about 4.5 m² of contact. The blade cannot be the force-transfer path; it vaporises before the target registers the hit. This is batch-wide wherever an S-Grade or higher figure is delivered through a held weapon.

options.option: Rule that the force is delivered by the working rather than through the steel, with the blade as the boundary marker only.
options.changes: Resolves it everywhere at once and matches the Glyph Index's account of what a working does; the blade becomes a pointer, not a lever.

options.option: Give weapons at these Grades a stated Durability or Aether-reinforcement rule that carries the load.
options.changes: A system addition affecting every armed practitioner; makes weapon quality matter and creates a new thing to break.

options.option: Read the Grade band as a whole-body or area output rather than a contact force.
options.changes: Purely interpretive, changes no page, and makes the benchmark tables mean something different everywhere.

options.option: Lower melee outputs to what a blade can carry and put the big numbers on area workings only.
options.changes: Large rebalancing; would separate armed and unarmed scaling for good.

quote_a: Field-wide override of one Wellspring's Core Law per verse, using the caster's own guilt, emotion, and memory as the fuel that authorises the override.
quote_b: A glyph cannot attack a law. Laws are not the sort of thing that can be opposed; the practitioner who tries is arguing with thermodynamics and will lose on schedule.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms.md
why: The sharpest off-system conflict in the batch. The working's stated Function is precisely the act the Master Glyph Index says cannot be performed. The page is internally coherent — Judicium supplies a verdict layer, and the Counterplay is an appellate move by a higher stratum — but it treats a Core Law as an instrument with an author rather than as a law.

options.option: Reread the working as boundary-moving rather than law-breaking: each verse imposes a limit under which the law's ordinary behaviour produces the stated result.
options.changes: Brings it inside the Index with no loss of drama; every verse then needs a stated boundary, which is real work and very findable for a player.

options.option: Rule that Wellspring Core Laws are amendable by a sufficient authority, and amend the Index accordingly.
options.changes: The largest change in the questionnaire: it would license law-editing as a class of working and affect Dirge Ascension too.

options.option: Recast the override as removing the practitioner's access to a Wellspring rather than altering the law — the law stands, the invocation fails.
options.changes: Much smaller effect, fully system-native, and consistent with Silence as the register already describes it.

options.option: Keep both texts and record the dispute as a live in-world disagreement about whether Core Laws are decree or nature.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the two positions become schools, which the lens in section 2 already frames.

quote_a: Fractura's refraction law
quote_b: Fractura gives the practitioner sight of those flaws
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The register's Fractura is about flaw populations and where a structure will fail; it is not a law of refraction. And the register's own reading is the better instrument for this working, because a flaw population is a distribution over where a thing will fail, so selecting which flaw carries the load is selecting which outcome happens. As written, Fractura is doing something the register does not describe.

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism using Fractura as flaw-sight, which makes it the working's natural engine.
options.changes: Better physics, better system fit, and it supports Reading B at SA-PHYS-PARALLAX-SUPERPOSITION-VS-SELECTION; the 'prismatic sheet' becomes appearance rather than mechanism.

options.option: Name the Wellspring that actually supplies refraction and add it to the page.
options.changes: Adds a Wellspring and a gate; keeps the visual signature intact.

options.option: Amend the register to give Fractura an optical aspect.
options.changes: A change to a Family page affecting every Fractura working in canon.

options.option: Rule that 'refraction' here is the school's metaphor for branch-splitting, not a law.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the word moves into the lens and the Mechanism is restated in flaw terms.

quote_a: Craft · Magicraft
quote_b: Nobody except the Accord says magicraft aloud. It is the examiner's category, the heading on a form. A practitioner asked what they do names their craft, never the umbrella.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: Four technique pages in this batch give their Craft as Magicraft — Ashfang Mark Invocation, Bloodbind Surge, Hunter's Breath and Cryost Ascendant. The Four Crafts page says Magicraft is the umbrella and the examiner's heading, not a craft anyone practises, and that the theoretical worker who studies Magicraft 'performs nothing'. Naming it as the Craft of a working leaves the working with no practised craft at all, and Law V's anchor rule is stated per craft.

options.option: Assign each of the four a real craft — Spellcraft, Runecraft or Draftcraft — as Maw of Crystalline Stasis already does.
options.changes: Four small edits; fixes Law V's anchor question for each and settles SA-CROSS-DRAVEN-CRAFT-SPLIT at the same time.

options.option: Rule that Magicraft is acceptable as a filing value on a Codex entry even though no practitioner says it.
options.changes: No edits; but the anchor rule then has nothing to attach to, and the distinction the Four Crafts page draws stops doing work.

options.option: Add a fifth craft covering bodily, self-directed workings, which is what all four of these are.
options.changes: A system addition, but these four pages are evidence that the taxonomy has a genuine hole in it.

options.option: Leave the field blank where the source does not support a craft.
options.changes: Honest and minimal; makes the gap visible on the wiki rather than papered over with the umbrella.

quote_a: Category · Synergia *(judgment call, unverified — see migration note)*
quote_b: A Synergia field is several Soul Crystals briefly sharing one Essence Core, Shell, and Layer, which is why Aqua-Typology souls anchor these fields most easily.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md
why: Synergia is defined as several Soul Crystals sharing one Core, Shell and Layer. Ashfang Mark Invocation is self-target, one Crystal, with a dead beast's residue as a template — there is no second Crystal to share anything with. The page flags its own assignment as an unverified judgment call, so this is a filing error the page half-admits.

options.option: Refile under a category for self-directed augmentation, naming which one the taxonomy supplies.
options.changes: One edit; needs a check against the Unified Taxonomy for the right heading.

options.option: Rule that a bound residue counts as a second party for Synergia purposes.
options.changes: Would make every Object-Wellspring working a Synergia, which is a large widening; connects to SA-GAP-ASHFANG-OBJECT-WELLSPRING.

options.option: Leave the category null until the taxonomy is checked.
options.changes: Keeps the honest flag the page already carries and removes the wrong value.

options.option: Amend the Synergia definition to include a living Crystal and a stored pattern.
options.changes: Changes a Magic System page and affects every Synergia entry in canon.

quote_a: Category · Mechanica *(judgment call, unverified — see migration note)*
quote_b: Mechanica always has a donor.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Mechanica Extraction Without Recognition.md
why: Mechanica is extraction without recognition and it always has a donor. Bloodbind Surge is Draven tearing open his own ancestral pact and flooding his own Shell; there is no donor and nothing is extracted from anyone. The page flags the assignment as an unverified judgment call.

options.option: Refile under a category for self-augmentation or Trait expression.
options.changes: One edit, and it stops a reader inferring a victim who does not exist.

options.option: Rule that the practitioner can be his own donor, making Mechanica available reflexively.
options.changes: Interesting and dark — it would make the Bloodbind a standing act of self-extraction — but it widens Mechanica considerably.

options.option: Leave the category null pending the taxonomy check.
options.changes: Minimal and honest.

options.option: Rule that the ancestral pact itself is the donor, with the Vorynn line as the extracted party.
options.changes: Keeps Mechanica, gives the working a genuinely unpleasant reading, and needs a ruling on whether a lineage can be a donor.

quote_a: Radius up to 60 m, centred on a point she can see or occupy; holds 5 turns or until shattered.
quote_b: Wards. Runecraft standing on a substrate, and therefore beaten the way Runecraft is beaten: damage the substrate.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md
why: The working is an inscribed lattice on ground and air — Runecraft in everything but duration — and yet it lasts five turns and cannot move with her. Runecraft in the register is a craft of standing inscriptions on substrates, with wards that persist for centuries and fail by having their substrate damaged. A written lattice that evaporates in fifteen seconds is either not Runecraft or Runecraft with a duration rule the system does not state.

options.option: Rule the Locus is Spellcraft that uses inscription as its anchor, not Runecraft.
options.changes: Keeps the substrate counter, explains the short duration as attention-bounded, and needs one edit.

options.option: State a Runecraft duration rule: an inscription holds as long as it is fed, and this one is fed by her presence.
options.changes: A system addition that would tidy every ephemeral inscription in canon and give Anchoring Debt a mechanism.

options.option: Make the lattice persist until broken, as a ward does, and rebalance around that.
options.changes: Much stronger working; the Anchoring Debt and the one-Locus-at-a-time limit become the whole cost.

options.option: Leave it and record that the batch has no duration rule for inscriptions.
options.changes: Records the gap; the account already flags the tension.

quote_a: Wellspring Vohrin (primary; carried in current canon by an existing Kharven card for this same frost-stasis phenomenon, though not itself on the Sixty's own enumerated list)
quote_b: VOHRIN · The Titan of Niflheim · Abyssal Depths · Entropy's peace, the settling of endings
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Fourteen Titans.md
why: Vohrin is named as a Wellspring by four technique pages and by Draven's own card, and it is not on the register's enumerated Sixty. It does appear in canon — as a Titan. Card and technique pages agree with each other and both disagree with the register and the Titans page. This is the batch's largest single conflict: it touches Hunter's Breath, Maw of Crystalline Stasis, Bloodbind Surge and Cryost Ascendant.

options.option: Add Vohrin to the Sixty as a Caloria cold-law current, with a Core Law written to match what the four pages already do.
options.changes: Settles four pages at once; requires a register edit and a name distinct from the Titan, or an explicit statement that they share one.

options.option: Rule that the Titan and the Wellspring are the same power at two strata, as the Correspondence Position would have it.
options.changes: No new Wellspring; makes four techniques Titan-derived, which raises their standing and probably their cost.

options.option: Refile all four workings under an attested Caloria cold current and drop the name.
options.changes: Four edits, no register change, and it costs Draven and Tovain a signature Wellspring.

options.option: Leave it unattested and record that the register is incomplete.
options.changes: No edits; every account that names Vohrin keeps its flag.

quote_a: Stage floor · Stage VI, Glory (Band D).
quote_b: Coherence Band
path_b: RULINGS.md
why: Nineteen accounts in this batch sit on pages or cards carrying a lettered Coherence Band. Lettered Coherence Bands are retired under R42, so every such line is a stale mechanic being quoted as current. The values are harmless where nothing depends on them and misleading where a reader takes them for a live gate.

options.option: Strip the lettered Band from every page and card that carries one.
options.changes: A sweep across nineteen files plus the cards; makes the retirement real, and is the only option that stops the confusion recurring.

options.option: Replace each Band with the live equivalent — Tier of Standing and η — where one can be derived.
options.changes: More work per file but leaves the reader with a usable number instead of a hole.

options.option: Leave them as historical annotations and mark them retired in place.
options.changes: Cheapest; keeps the archaeology visible, which has its own value for a document-driven setting.

options.option: Rule that Bands remain valid for pages written before R42 and are simply not used going forward.
options.changes: No edits, but then two systems are live at once and a reader cannot tell which applies.

quote_a: Stage floor · Stage VI, Glory (Band D).
quote_b: Coherence Band
path_b: RULINGS.md
why: The specific instance on this page: the FOW line gives a Band D alongside the Stage floor. Band D is a retired lettered Coherence Band (R42) and nothing on the page depends on it. Recorded separately from the batch-wide item so the page can be fixed without waiting for the sweep.

options.option: Delete the parenthetical Band from the FOW line.
options.changes: One-word edit, no mechanical consequence.

options.option: Replace it with Tier of Standing 5 · Expert and η 0.50–0.60, derived from Stage VI.
options.changes: Gives the reader a live figure in place of a dead one.

options.option: Leave it, marked retired.
options.changes: Consistent with whatever is decided for the batch-wide sweep.

quote_a: Stage floor · Stage VIII, Transcendence (Band B).
quote_b: Coherence Band
path_b: RULINGS.md
why: As above, on this page: a lettered Band B retired under R42, quoted in the FOW line beside a live Stage. Recorded separately so the page can be corrected independently.

options.option: Delete the parenthetical Band.
options.changes: One-word edit.

options.option: Replace with Tier 6 · Master and η 0.70–0.80, derived from Stage VIII.
options.changes: Live figures, and they agree with her card's η of 0.70.

options.option: Leave it, marked retired.
options.changes: Defers to the batch-wide decision.

quote_a: The source gives no date or founding problem for Lumen Dissecans beyond Serenyra's own authorship. It reads as a working built for the same analytic practice as her other entries, aimed specifically at active hostile or defensive magic rather than at people. No location is given beyond the Iridescent Archive filing destination, unattested in current canon; Thesauriel, the archive the technique's outcomes feed into, is likewise unattested and kept because the card names it as where the readings go.
quote_b: **Thesauriel, the Mirror Codex** · *Compendium-focus.* **Writes complex lattices directly into reality without verbal incantation.** *Runecraft in a book.*
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:96
why: CORRECTED IN THIS BATCH; the row was filed on a false premise and its id keeps the UNATT prefix only so the citations in the Lumen Dissecans and Speculum Recordatio accounts continue to resolve. Thesauriel is not unattested. Serenyra's card names it twice - as 'Thesauriel, the Mirror Codex, Compendium-focus. Writes complex lattices directly into reality without verbal incantation. Runecraft in a book', and again in her Craft line, 'Runecraft first, Spellcraft second. Thesauriel writes lattices directly into reality without verbal incantation.' The real conflict is what it is. The card makes it an instrument: a compendium-focus, a book, the substrate a Runecraft working stands on. Lumen Dissecans makes it a place - 'the archive the technique's outcomes feed into', a filing destination whose readings are stored - and declares it 'likewise unattested'. Speculum Recordatio uses the card's reading and treats it as the instrument that takes the imprint and holds the ward. The difference is mechanical rather than descriptive, because the Counterplay register's answer to Runecraft is 'damage the substrate': if Thesauriel is a book in her hands it is a counter anyone can reach, and if it is an archive elsewhere it is not. The Iridescent Archive, named in the same Lumen Dissecans sentence, is genuinely unattested and is page-declared; that part of the original row stands and is recorded rather than logged.

options.option: Rule the card's reading canon: Thesauriel is a compendium-focus she carries, and correct Lumen Dissecans' Origin line to match.
options.changes: Makes the substrate reachable and gives every Serenyra Runecraft page the same counter; costs Lumen Dissecans its 'file it into Thesauriel' consequence, which needs somewhere for readings to go.

options.option: Rule it is both: a codex she carries whose contents are an archive, so filing a reading into it and writing a lattice out of it are the same act.
options.changes: Reconciles both pages without losing either function, and makes capturing the book equivalent to capturing the archive, which is a larger consequence than either page intends.

options.option: Split the name: the codex keeps Thesauriel and the archive gets a different one.
options.changes: Cleanest mechanically and creates a name, which no issue has asked for.

options.option: Leave both readings standing and treat the instrument and the archive as separate things that share a name.
options.changes: No edits; leaves 'damage the substrate' pointing at two different objects depending on which page the table reads.

quote_a: 2,800,000 AU/s output, as given.
quote_b: her established 22 AU/s baseline
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Lumen Dissecans.md
why: The batch contains exactly two sourced AU/s figures and they sit six Stages and five orders of magnitude apart with no scaling rule between them. Every other AU/s and Flux Density figure in the batch is derived from one or the other, so the absence of a ladder is load-bearing for the whole set.

options.option: State an AU/s progression by Stage or by Tier of Standing.
options.changes: Would let every page in the batch derive its own output instead of inheriting one of two anchors; the single most useful system addition the batch asks for.

options.option: Rule that AU/s is a per-practitioner sheet value with no Stage relation at all.
options.changes: No new rule; but then every page without a card keeps a null and the two anchors stop being comparable.

options.option: Anchor the ladder on these two figures and interpolate.
options.changes: Cheap and immediately usable; risks fossilising two numbers that were never meant to define a curve.

options.option: Rule the Zenith figure is not commensurable with lower-Stage output, per Part Four's caution.
options.changes: Consistent with SA-NUM-ZENITH-CONVENTIONAL-METRICS; leaves 22 AU/s as the only usable anchor.

quote_a: Absolute Crystal
path_a: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md
quote_b: Crystal State
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md

Whether an Ashfang talon is one, or merely a residue-bearing focus, is a filing question the page does not answer — and it changes what happens when a talon is taken off him, whether it can be used by anyone else, and whether it registers to detection.

The page prices both modes identically and the system gives no ratio between a forward and a reverse working. So the Worldbind mode is either much more expensive than the Worldrend mode or the books do not balance.

If it is architectural then it is fixed wherever he goes and no terrain touches it. Which one is true decides whether a fourth construct is ever possible and whether Silence reduces the count.

path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md

These constructs explicitly do not need continuous input once formed, so whether a Silence unmakes them, prevents new ones, or does nothing at all is genuinely undecided — and it is the difference between the cheapest counter working and not working.

options.option: Rule Silence prevents summoning but does not unmake a standing construct.

quote_a: The blow that lands is real. The shape throwing it is a memory wearing a body it never had.
quote_b: Anamnesis's law is remanent magnetisation and thermoluminescent dosimetry ... Oblivara's law is retroreflection: a corner-reflector geometry returns incident information precisely along the path it arrived on.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Mireglass Suffusion.md
why: The Mechanism names two information laws and no force-bearing law. Remanent magnetisation returns a record; retroreflection returns incident energy along its own vector. Neither supplies mass or momentum, and the page has no Eidolyn-style templated-nucleation clause of the kind the Oneiron pages use to give a construct solidity. The arithmetic makes the gap checkable: at the page's own B-Grade floor a delivered attack is 1.046x10^9 J (Part Eleven), and the entire energy reservoir inside a 12-15 m field against one standing target is about 4.2x10^8 J (1.1x10^6 J of retroreflectable daylight over 24 s, 5.0x10^7 J of air sensible heat at 30 K, and 3.7x10^8 J of one adult's adipose store). That is short by a factor of 2.5, and only clears with three or more targets in the field, i.e. by spending them. Read instead as an ordinary strike of 100-200 J the account closes with four orders to spare. The page does not say which it means.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the silhouette does not strike, and the working's whole output is the attention-split and clarity loss the Target Response already states.
options.changes: Removes the damage line; makes the Suffusion a control and destabilisation working, which its governing Sub-Stat (Harmonics Attunement) already suits; strengthens the Judicium counter, since recognition then ends the working completely.

options.changes: Adds a Wellspring to the Codex line, a fourth Sub-Stat to the FOW line, a second Path gate to check, and probably a second cost; makes the working more expensive at a Stage VI floor.

options.option: State the blow's yield explicitly at ordinary-strike scale (100-200 J) and detach it from the B-Grade band.
options.changes: Smallest change; the Grade requirement becomes a gate on the field's reach and read, not on its damage, and the account closes.

page: (5 pages: Mireglass Suffusion, Nightglass Seal, Oneiron Parasite, Principle Overwrite, Spinal Forge Ascent)
quote_a: Duration once flooded: four exchanges, roughly twenty-four seconds
quote_b: Duration approximately 20 seconds per sustained watch (estimate, converted from the source's "4 turns")
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Oneiron Parasite · Nightmare Warden.md
why: A third turn-length convention is now in use. SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH records 3 s per turn on the Drakvor and Draven pages and 5 s per turn on the Francis and Aeldoris pages. The two Iridescent Archive pages in this batch convert at 6 s per turn: Mireglass Suffusion gives four exchanges as about twenty-four seconds and Nightglass Seal gives two exchanges as about twelve. Principle Overwrite states its rate outright as 5 s per turn. So the same unit is being converted at 3, 5 and 6 seconds inside one Techniques volume, a spread of two to one, and every duration in the batch inherits it.

options.option: Rule one turn length for the whole system and restate every converted duration.
options.changes: One ruling; roughly twenty durations across the Techniques volume change, some by a factor of two; the batch's derived EU-per-use figures move with them.

options.option: Rule that turn counts are not convertible and state durations only in seconds on every page.
options.changes: Removes the ambiguity permanently; requires an author decision per page rather than an arithmetic pass.

options.option: Keep turns as the unit and publish a conversion table by Stage or by Grade, so a faster practitioner's turn is shorter.
options.changes: Makes the spread a feature and ties duration to Dexterity; adds a table and a new check to every page.

options.option: Record the three conventions and leave every affected duration as a range.
options.changes: No change; every duration in the volume stays ambiguous by up to two to one.

quote_a: Tenebra applies both to the Shell. Its practitioners are not invisible. They are quieter than the background, which is better.
path_a: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
quote_b: a corner reflector returns incident energy precisely along the path it arrived on
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: The pane is one surface running both currents at once. Tenebra's law requires absorption plus 'shaping surfaces so the little that reflects goes anywhere except back at the observer'; Oblivara's requires return 'precisely along the path it arrived on'. Those are opposite geometric requirements. A retroreflective surface is the brightest object in the field to whoever is illuminating it and invisible to everyone else, which is the worst possible geometry for the stealth half and is exactly what Tenebra's own failure line ('observed from the one direction they did not plan for returns a very bright signal indeed') warns about. The page's Target Response confirms the return is live, and its own Counter then exploits it. Either the contradiction is the working's deliberate weakness or it is unnoticed.

options.option: Rule the contradiction deliberate: the pane is dark to the room and a beacon to whoever probes it, and that is its stated weakness.
options.changes: Costs nothing and makes the page sharper; the Judicium counter becomes the mechanically obvious one and the pane becomes dangerous to raise against an illuminating opponent.

options.option: Separate the two functions in space: an absorptive outer layer and a retroreflective inner face.
options.changes: Adds structure and a second failure mode (which layer was struck); needs a sentence in the Mechanism and probably a higher cost.

options.option: Drop the retroreflective half and run the pane on Tenebra alone plus Oblivara's error correction only.
options.changes: Loses the 'smear where a face should be' Target Response; simplifies the working and weakens the Judicium counter.

options.option: Rule that Oblivara's return applies to authorization patterns only and not to light or Essence-sight.
options.changes: Keeps both currents; requires a statement about what 'incident information' means for Oblivara generally, which affects every Oblivara page.

quote_a: Governing Primary · Gnosis (Cognition, the Sub-Stat governing resistance to conceptual erasure and perceptual misdirection), secondary Resilience (Insulation).
quote_b: Fortification requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B; resistance to self-generated blowback is open.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Under the Merge Ledger (Part Twelve) Resilience Insulation reads as Resilience Fortification. Fortification above B-Grade requires Body Path at Stage IV. The working requires A-Grade, which exceeds B, and the page's declared Path gate is 'Spirit, secondary Fate' with no Body Path at any weight. Gnosis Cognition's gate does close against the declared Spirit Path, so only the secondary Sub-Stat fails.

options.option: Add Body as a tertiary Path gate on the page.
options.changes: One line; implies a practitioner who has done physical work, which sits oddly with a purely reactive shadow working.

options.option: Change the secondary Sub-Stat to Resilience Persistence, whose gate is Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed S and which the declared secondary Fate Path would carry.
options.changes: Re-reads the pane's endurance as Fate-anchored rather than insulating, which fits a working that attacks authorization; changes what a counter targets.

options.option: Rule that only the governing Sub-Stat's gates bind a technique page, not secondary ones.
options.changes: Settles a large number of pathgate rows across the volume at once; weakens Part Seven's stated strict reading.

options.option: Note that Fortification's self-generated-blowback component is open and rule that this working uses only that component.
options.changes: Smallest change; requires the page to say the pane insulates him from his own erasure rather than from incoming force.

quote_a: Basilithe's crystal-growth law is pushed into a metastable high-order lattice
quote_b: A body's resonant frequency is fixed by its stiffness and its mass, and a high-stiffness low-loss structure holds that frequency against forcing so reliably that civilisations set their clocks by cut quartz. Basilithe raises the Crystal's stiffness until its resonance simply will not be driven off, which is a defence against every technique that works by imposing an external rhythm.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The register's Basilithe is a resonance-stability current: natural frequency, stiffness-to-mass ratio, quartz oscillator stability. It contains no growth law. The page attributes a crystal-growth law to it and builds the Obelisk's lattice on that attribution. The register's actual law would serve the working better, since holding a configuration against forcing is what the Obelisk does for its whole duration and a quartz habit is a prism, but it also imports a failure the page does not carry: 'Resonant catastrophe. A frequency that cannot be shifted also cannot be detuned away from a forcing that happens to match it.'

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism to use Basilithe's stated resonance-stability law, with resonant catastrophe as the named failure.
options.changes: One paragraph; gives the Obelisk a precise, findable counter (match its locked frequency) and explains the prism habit; makes the Weakness line about radiance secondary.

options.option: Add a growth current to the Codex line and keep Basilithe for the holding, e.g. a Materia crystallisation Wellspring from the register.
options.changes: Adds a sixth or seventh Wellspring to a working that already runs six; raises the Tempering Capacity problem (SA-GAP-OPALIS-TEMPERING-CAPACITY) further.

options.option: Amend the Basilithe register entry to include a growth law.
options.changes: Changes a Core Law, which affects every Basilithe page including Harmonic Null-Ascension; the Families page's physical readings are built to be one law each.

options.option: Record the attribution as loose language and rule that 'crystal-growth' is shorthand for the metastable lattice the resonance law holds.
options.changes: No content change; leaves the resonant-catastrophe counter unwritten.

quote_a: Tarturon's entropy law is throttled to run backward across the Obelisk's own surface, a local, temporary entropy inversion
quote_b: Below yield a material returns to shape and the load leaves no record. Above it, behaviour changes kind, and the response scales with the load applied rather than with anything the material chose. Tarturon couples output to moral weight through exactly that curve, and like thermite it supplies its own oxidiser, which is the mechanical reason the reaction cannot be smothered once initiated.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The register's Tarturon is a yield-criterion and self-oxidising-reaction current coupled to moral weight. It is not an entropy current. Entropy of mixing belongs to Dissolution, The Unbinding Stream, in Limina: 'a solid dissolves not because the solvent attacks it but because the mixed state has higher entropy than the separated one'. The page uses Tarturon for the entropy inversion and then names 'raw Tarturon or a comparable Dissolution-aligned field' as the counter, treating the two as interchangeable. Tarturon's actual failure line is meanwhile the best available explanation of the page's own four-instance cap and goes unused: 'Runaway.
