path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings.md:164
why: Ten Wellsprings across five Families: Vectoria (Fractura, Petralon, Penance), Caloria (Cataclysm), Limina (Dissolution, Tenebra, Oneirion), Materia (Basilithe, Tarturon) and Fulguria (Orrenthal). That is the heaviest conduit load in this batch by a wide margin, and it contains the system's own named canonical hard case three times over - Basilithe and Tarturon on the Materia side against Dissolution, Tenebra and Oneirion on the Limina side. The system requires the tension to be resolved and names exactly two routes, Temperance advancement or a Compound Trait holding the contradiction as a single law, and the page states neither. Stage XII is high advancement and may well be the answer, but the page does not say so and no Compound Trait is on file because Opalis has no card at all. The ceiling is also unpriceable: 'The ceiling is Tempering Capacity and it is not negotiable. Exceeding it does not fail gracefully by dropping the newest harmonization. It degrades all active harmonizations equally', and no Tempering Capacity figure exists for anyone in the corpus. So the working with the largest harmonization load in the batch is the one whose load cannot be checked against any ceiling, and whose hardest internal contradiction is left unaddressed.

options.option: State on the page that Stage XII advancement is what holds the Materia-Limina tension, naming the clause.
options.changes: Closes the gap with one line and makes the Stage floor load-bearing for a second reason; implies the working is impossible below Stage XII for a structural reason rather than a power one, which is a better limit than the one the page gives.

options.option: Give Opalis a Compound Trait that holds the contradiction as a single law, which is the system's other named route.
options.changes: Gives the working a named mechanism and Opalis her defining Trait, and would be the most interesting single addition to the page; requires a card, which does not exist.

options.option: Reduce the Wellspring stack so the Materia and Limina sides do not co-occur, keeping Fractura, Cataclysm and Dissolution.
options.changes: Removes the hard case and most of the Breadth-clause problem at once, and costs the page the Basilithe reading its own Weakness depends on, since Basilithe is currently both a component and the counter.

options.option: Publish Tempering Capacity figures, or a formula, so a ten-harmonization working can be checked against a ceiling.
options.changes: Answers this page and every other multi-harmonization working; a system-level addition that would immediately put some existing builds over the line.

quote_a: **Target Response** · The chosen wound is pinned into place; an escape technique whose success would require an outcome the Lance has already removed from the possibility set simply does not produce that outcome.
quote_b: The ratio varies. At F through D, Durability sits at roughly seventy to eighty percent of Strike Force yield, so a clean peer hit penetrates but is not catastrophic. At A through S, the ratio narrows to sixty to seventy percent, reflecting denser Shell architecture but also more lethal focused technique. At SSS and above it widens again to roughly fifty percent, because the energy differential between a clean hit and survival is so vast that the Crystal's priority shifts from absorption to avoidance, Domain manipulation and reality-grade countermeasures.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:102
why: Part Eleven states that at SSS and above absorption stops being viable and survival runs through three modes: avoidance, Domain manipulation, and reality-grade countermeasures. This working deletes the first of the three by construction - an escape whose success requires an outcome the selection has spent 'simply does not produce that outcome' - which is not a strong defence beaten but a defensive category removed. The working is not unfair on the whole, and the account records that: it leaves the other two modes open and the page names counters in both, a pure Basilithe anchor being Domain-side and probability-flattening being reality-grade, and four of its five stated counters need no peer. Two further things weigh in its favour, and one against. In its favour, the page's structural limit is arithmetic rather than fiat - a flaw-free target offers nothing to select, worth two orders of magnitude on the real materials - and its tell is a deliberate aimed gesture. Against it, the page omits the best cost it has: Fractura's own register failure, 'Self-inspection. The Wellspring does not exempt its bearer, and a Fractura practitioner under strain reads their own flaw population with perfect clarity at the worst possible moment', which for a Stage XII practitioner holding ten currents at 900 m is a genuine hazard the system supplies free. So the fairness question is narrow: is deleting avoidance at the Grade where avoidance is the primary defence acceptable when the cost that should balance it is left unstated.

options.option: State Fractura's Self-inspection failure as a cost of the working, with a stated trigger under strain or on a second cast.
options.changes: Balances the deletion of avoidance with a real in-scene hazard and costs nothing to invent, since the register already supplies it; makes a second cast frightening rather than merely expensive, which the page's escalating-cost clause already wants.

options.option: Narrow the deletion: the selection removes one escape route rather than the outcome class, so avoidance is degraded rather than deleted.
options.changes: Restores avoidance as a viable mode at the Grade where Part Eleven says it must be, and weakens the working's signature effect, which is precisely that escape stops working.

options.option: Require the selection to be made before the target commits, so a target who moves first has not yet had an outcome spent.
options.changes: Turns the working into a timing contest and gives a skilled opponent a real play, which is the fairest version; needs the ordering stated, and makes the 900 m range matter in a new way.

options.option: Accept the deletion as the point of a Stage XII signature working and leave the costs as written.
options.changes: Keeps the working intact and leaves one defensive mode closed at the Grade where the system says it is primary, with no stated cost balancing it; the strongest reading is that the four non-peer counters already carry the fairness load.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Range up to 900 m, single-target with a fractured echo along a line up to 40 m; at the required SSS-Grade the strike sits at the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark, on the order of 1 PN of peak force and roughly 400 TJ of yield (low hundred-kiloton TNT-equivalent), an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives no force figure of its own. Resolution is instantaneous, with the harmonic disturbance it leaves lingering a few seconds afterward.
quote_b: **Numerical Effect** · A static field 3 to 7 m around the caster, holding for an estimated three sustained exchanges of incoming pressure, on the order of ten to fifteen seconds continuous, an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives duration only in the old system's "turns."
path_b: wiki/Techniques/The Aether Bastion.md:39
why: Four technique pages cite 'Law Two' as the authority under which an estimate was chosen - Sovereign Parallax Lance, Celestial Harmonic Shear, Harmonic Null-Ascension and The Aether Bastion - and no Law Two is defined anywhere in the corpus. There is no such entry in The Four Crafts, where the numbered Laws live and where Law V and Law III are both discussed by number, none in the Core Vocabulary, none in RULINGS.md, and no occurrence of the string outside those four Numerical Effect lines. This is load-bearing rather than decorative: on each of the four pages Law Two is the stated justification for the only numbers the page gives, and on three of them the number it justifies is the identical 'on the order of 1 PN peak force and roughly 400 TJ yield' - which is below the SSS floor of 418 TJ. So a figure that is wrong on three pages is wrong in the same way each time, on the authority of a rule a reader cannot find and therefore cannot check. A player following the lookup trail stops at the citation.

options.option: Publish Law Two as a real rule for how a missing figure is estimated - presumably 'take the conservative low end of the Grade's benchmark band' - and place it where the numbered Laws live.
options.changes: Makes four pages checkable and gives the corpus a stated convention for estimating absent numbers, which many pages need; would immediately show that three of the four estimates were taken just below the band rather than at its low end.

options.option: Strike the citation and state the estimates as estimates, with the band they were drawn from cited directly to Part Eleven.
options.changes: Removes an unfindable authority and points the reader at the real table; leaves four pages with unattributed figures, which is more honest than a false attribution but less useful than a rule.

options.option: Replace it with the existing convention it seems to mean, citing Part Eleven's Strike Force table and the Focused-Yield Principle by name on each page.
options.changes: Ties each estimate to the clause that actually governs it, and would have caught the 400 TJ error at the point of writing; four page edits.

options.option: Leave it and record that Law Two is a drafting shorthand with no register entry.
options.changes: Costs nothing and leaves the only stated justification for the numbers on four pages pointing at nothing, on pages whose numbers are wrong.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · An Overchannel-class release: stored force discharges at two to five times what a single sustainable S-Grade impact would otherwise produce (the documented Overchannel spike range at any Tier), spent all at once across an eight-metre radius rather than sustained.
quote_b: **Target Response** · Everyone inside the radius staggers and loses footing; the release reads as a single sudden iron-crack rather than a sustained push.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Sovereign's Reprisal.md:40
why: The page's own arithmetic, carried out, does not produce the effect the page describes, and the gap is about 400,000 to one. Part Eleven's S row gives a sustainable impact of 4.184-24.3 TJ, and the page releases two to five times that, so 8.4-121.5 TJ. Knocking a standing person off balance takes roughly 20-35 kPa of incident overpressure; under Hopkinson-Cranz scaling Z = R/W^(1/3), 20 kPa sits near Z = 5, so at 8 m the charge is (8/5)^3 = 4 kg TNT or about 17 MJ, and 35 kPa needs about 12 kg or 50 MJ. So a stagger at 8 m costs 2e7 J and the page banks 8.4e12 J at its floor. The consequences are not marginal. 8.4 TJ is 2.0 kt, whose fireball radius is about 90 x 2^0.4 = 120 m with Drakvor standing at its centre and the crowd the page calls 'the worst possible formation against him' inside it. The page also routes the discharge 'through his spine', and 0.1% coupling of 8.4 TJ is 8.4 GJ against a roughly 1.2 MJ margin to a lethal core temperature, which is seven thousand times fatal; no coupling fraction is stated. Read the other way, a 20 MJ release is below Part Eleven's B-Grade floor of 1.046 GJ, so the described effect sits five to six Grades under the working's stated Grade. Everything else about the working's geometry checks: the 8 m radius is inside Part Eleven's S-Grade Contact Range of 5-15 m, and the 2-5x Overchannel multiplier is correctly cited. Only the magnitude fails, and it fails in the direction of turning a non-lethal crowd-control working into a tactical nuclear device.

options.option: State the release as an absolute figure matched to the stated effect - tens of megajoules across 8 m - and drop the 'two to five times an S-Grade impact' framing.
options.changes: Makes the working do what the page says it does and keeps every other number intact; puts the release five or six Grades below the practitioner's Grade, which needs a stated reason - most naturally that the banked quantity is the attacker's impulse and not his own Grade's output.

options.option: Rule that the banked quantity is whatever was actually delivered by the incoming blows rather than a multiple of the defender's own Grade ceiling, so the release scales with what the enemy spent.
options.changes: Solves the magnitude at a stroke, makes the working's output depend on the opposition rather than on Drakvor, and makes the page's Consequence line exactly true: a mob really does arm his counter, in proportion. Removes Overchannel from the mechanism, which the page currently uses as its only numeric anchor.

options.option: Keep 8.4-121.5 TJ and state the real consequences: a kiloton-class detonation centred on the practitioner, lethal to everything inside a hundred metres including him.
options.changes: Physically consistent and turns the working into a last-resort suicide option rather than a crowd-control move; contradicts the Target Response, the Consequence and the Cost lines, all of which describe a survivable event.

options.option: Rule that an Overchannel release deposits its energy only into the momentum of bodies within the radius, with no coupling to air or ground and none back into the practitioner.
options.changes: Preserves every figure on the page by exempting the working from blast physics and from its own stated discharge path; needs a general rule about what Overchannel releases couple to, which would apply to every Overchannel working in the corpus.

quote_a: *Unattested in current canon*: Drakvor, and the harness itself as a named artefact; no entry for it exists outside this card.
quote_b: **Stage VIII — Transcendence** · **Level 295** · Level Band III · Coherence Band B · Grade S · Ceiling 550.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Drakvor · The Black-Crowned Bastion.md:60
why: The page declares its own practitioner unattested and the card is in the corpus at wiki/Volume I - Character Cards/Drakvor - The Black-Crowned Bastion.md, with a full sheet: Stage VIII Transcendence, Level 295, Grade S, ceiling 550, Aether Shell Class V Radiant, Crystal State 'Refined, overbuilt by design', eta ~0.55 rising above 0.8 in tuned bastions, and Path 'Body dominant, Spirit secondary, Attraction minor, Fate carried only by the Domain'. The second half of the claim is false too: the card names the harness twice, as 'the Aegis Rib plates' in his Build line and as 'the Aegis Rib harness' in his Risk line, and the Risk line independently states this technique's cost - 'Over-bracing a field sends strain back into his own bones and the Aegis Rib harness.' This matters beyond tidiness. Because the card exists, every Path gate, eta figure and Stage claim on this page becomes checkable, and two of them then fail; because the page says it does not exist, the account would otherwise have had to leave all of them null. A reader who believes the page stops looking.

options.option: Strike the unattested note and cite the card, so the page's Path gate and eta claims are checked against the sheet.
options.changes: Makes the page auditable and immediately surfaces the two Path-gate misses and the eta band problem; costs nothing but the one line.

options.option: Strike the note and also name the harness as the Aegis Rib, matching the card's own term.
options.changes: Ties the technique to a named artefact already in canon and gives the substrate counter something concrete to break; commits the harness to whatever the card says about it.

options.option: Keep the note as a record of when the page was written and add a dated correction beneath it.
options.changes: Preserves the drafting history, which may matter for other stale unattested notes in the corpus; leaves a false statement on the page for a reader who reads only the first line.

options.option: Audit the corpus for other 'unattested in current canon' notes that have since been overtaken by cards.
options.changes: Likely finds more of these - the same note pattern appears on other technique pages - and turns a single-page fix into a sweep; a separate piece of work from this batch.

quote_a: **Governing Primary and Sub-Stats** · Gnosis Acuity and Gnosis Analysis (Judicium's stated strengths, reading the threshold); Tempering Yield and Harmonics Stability (Cinerion's stated strengths, banking and stabilising the residue before release).
quote_b: **Fortification** — Compressing incoming hostile Essence and redirecting it through internal structure rather than absorbing it as damage, and resistance to self-generated blowback from Overchannel rebound and interrupted high-tier workings. Converting a wound, or a mistake, into something the Crystal can metabolise.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:93
why: Part Twelve defines Resilience Fortification as this working, in three clauses, and the page's Sub-Stat list does not contain it. Compressing incoming hostile Essence and redirecting it through internal structure rather than absorbing it as damage is the banking. Resistance to self-generated blowback from Overchannel rebound is the page's own stated Cost, spinal recoil on an Overchannel-class release. Converting a wound into something the Crystal can metabolise is Drakvor's own framing, 'Impact is tribute'. The omission is explicable and that is what makes it worth ruling: the page's four Sub-Stats derive exactly from what its two Wellsprings strengthen once the Merge Ledger is applied - Judicium gives Gnosis Acuity and Analysis, Cinerion gives Tempering Yield and Harmonics Stability - so the FOW line was built by asking what the Wellsprings strengthen and never by asking what the working does. Adding Fortification costs nothing mechanically: its gate is 'Fortification requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B', the page declares Body Path, and the card gives Body dominant at Stage VIII, so it passes cleanly.

options.option: Add Resilience Fortification to the page's Sub-Stat list as the working's central Sub-Stat, with the other four supporting it.
options.changes: Makes the page's architecture describe the page's mechanic, passes its own gate with no other change, and gives a player a single Sub-Stat to look up; implies the working scales with Fortification rather than with Tempering Yield, which changes what a build for it looks like.

options.option: Rule generally that a technique's Sub-Stat list must name the Sub-Stats its mechanic uses, not only those its Wellsprings strengthen.
options.changes: Would correct this page and probably many others, since deriving from Stat Effect lines is clearly the house method; a corpus-wide audit rather than one edit.

options.option: Leave the list and note that Fortification is implied by the Resilience layer without being named.
options.changes: Cheapest; leaves the one Sub-Stat that a player would search for absent from the page they would search on.

options.option: Reconsider whether Fortification rather than Cinerion is the working's real basis, and rebuild the Codex line accordingly.
options.changes: Might simplify the page to one Family and one Wellspring plus a Sub-Stat, which is cleaner; costs the Cinerion reading, and with it the Fouling answer to the page's own open question.

quote_a: **Path gate** · Body
quote_b: **Perception** open. **Acuity** requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C. **Forecast** requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed S. **Fluency** requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D and Stage III to exceed C, with its Command Weight component requiring Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C. **Retention** requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Stage VI to exceed A for the number of complete workings held loaded. **Analysis** open, though diagnosis of external fields and living beings requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B. **Cognition** open, though resistance to glamour and psychic misdirection requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B. **Vigilance** open.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:126
why: The page declares Body Path alone and two of its four Sub-Stats are Spirit-gated at Grades this working exceeds. Gnosis Acuity requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C, and the working is S-Grade. Gnosis Analysis is open but its clause for 'diagnosis of external fields and living beings' requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B, and reading the force of an incoming blow is diagnosis of an external field - it is the page's own stated Judicium function. Tempering Yield does require Body Path at Stage III to exceed C, so the declared Path is right for one of the four. The practitioner is not the problem: his card gives 'Body dominant, Spirit secondary', so Drakvor satisfies both gates and only the page's declaration is wrong. But the card also exposes a hole the page never mentions. Harmonics Stability is open except that 'holding resonance in Wellspring-absent ground requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed S', and the card says 'Fate carried only by the Domain' - so on Aether-thin ground outside his own Domain he lacks the Path that stabilises the banked residue before release, which is a real and findable condition under which the working degrades.

options.option: Declare Body and Spirit on the page, matching the card, and note the Fate condition on Harmonics Stability.
options.changes: Makes the page agree with its practitioner and with Part Seven, and hands players the Wellspring-absent-ground counter explicitly; two lines.

options.option: Declare Body and Spirit but leave the Fate condition unstated, as a counter for players to find.
options.changes: Fixes the gates and keeps the best counter on the lookup trail rather than on the page, which is what the fair-play brief asks for; relies on the card and Part Seven both being read.

options.option: Rule that a technique's Path gate names the Path that delivers the working, with Sub-Stat gates checked against the practitioner's sheet instead.
options.changes: Reconciles this page and most other Path-gate conflicts in the batch by making the two statements answer different questions; needs the sheet-side check written down somewhere or the gates stop being checked.

options.option: Replace the two Gnosis Sub-Stats with open or Body-gated ones so Body alone suffices.
options.changes: Preserves the single-Path declaration; removes the threshold-reading function that is the whole reason Judicium is on the page, and with it the page's account of why the release is deliberate rather than reflexive.

quote_a: **Weakness** · Piercing strikes concentrate force into an area too small to trip the harness's threshold cleanly, and a ranged harasser never lets Drakvor bank anything worth releasing.
quote_b: **Trigger** · Reactive. The harness activates automatically on impact above a threshold force; Drakvor does not have to call it, only choose when to release what it has taken.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Sovereign's Reprisal.md:36
why: The page's only two counters both depend on what the threshold measures, and it gives two incompatible answers. The Trigger line says 'a threshold force'; the Weakness line says a piercing strike fails because its area is 'too small'. Force and area together are pressure, and a threshold reading pressure would be tripped far more easily by a spike, not less - a spike at 1 mm2 and a fist at 100 cm2 delivering the same force differ in pressure by a factor of a million. The page's stated weakness is only correct if the threshold reads total impulse, and on impulse it is correct and interesting: a 1 kg hammer head at 20 m/s carries 20 kg.m/s and 200 J, while a 10 g bullet at 800 m/s carries 8 kg.m/s and 3,200 J, so the hammer delivers two and a half times the momentum with one sixteenth of the energy, and a piercing strike that passes through transfers only the momentum it loses. So the physics supports the page's conclusion by a route the page does not state, and contradicts the route it does state. The system supplies no rule for what a Runecraft trigger threshold measures, which leaves the working's counterability resting on an unstated choice between force, pressure and impulse.

options.option: State that the threshold reads total impulse, and let the piercing and ranged counters follow from momentum transfer.
options.changes: Makes the page's two counters correct and derivable, and gives players a real handle - anything that transfers little momentum is safe to use on him; means a very light, very fast strike is safe while a slow shoulder-check is not, which is counterintuitive at the table and worth the page saying out loud.

options.option: State that it reads pressure, and rewrite the Weakness: a spike trips it easily and banks almost nothing, so the counter is that it wastes the harness's charge rather than evading it.
options.changes: Keeps the Trigger line's 'force over an area' reading and inverts the counter into something arguably better - baiting the harness into banking nothing - but contradicts the page's explicit statement that the technique cannot be baited into firing on nothing.

options.option: Publish a general rule for Runecraft trigger thresholds - what quantity they measure and how a threshold is stated - applicable to every reactive inscription in the corpus.
options.changes: Closes this gap and any other reactive-ward page; a system-level addition that would need to cover pressure, impulse, energy and Essence-flux triggers separately.

options.option: Leave it and mark the page's two counters as stated conclusions without a derivable basis.
options.changes: Costs nothing and leaves a working whose only counters cannot be reasoned to from the rules, which fails the lookup-trail standard even though the counters themselves are named.

quote_a: **Cost** · Spinal Aether recoil and brief vertigo on every release. The discharge path runs through Drakvor's own body, not around it, and an Overchannel-range release is not free simply because it started as someone else's hit.
quote_b: **Overchannel Spikes.** The benchmarks above are sustainable output. Overchannel can temporarily spike Strike Force and Lifting Strength by **two to five times** the sustainable ceiling, depending on the Ardency Overchannel Sub-Stat's Grade and the character's tolerance for Crystal Fracture risk. Every Overchannel event deposits structural damage that must be healed through rest, alchemical treatment or Temperance advancement. A character who regularly Overchannels accumulates fracture density that eventually becomes permanent. Some fractures become architectural features. Most become liabilities.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:152
why: The page takes its output from this clause and stops reading at the multiplier. It cites 'the documented Overchannel spike range at any Tier' for its two-to-five times release, which is accurate, and then prices the whole cost as spinal recoil and a few seconds of vertigo. The same clause states the price: every Overchannel event deposits structural damage requiring rest, alchemical treatment or Temperance advancement to heal, and regular Overchannelling accumulates fracture density that eventually becomes permanent. Part Seven adds that Overchannel carries 'inherent Overflow risk above D-Grade and Backlash risk above C, with no Path providing structural protection', so at S-Grade the risk is both mandatory and unmitigable by Path - and this working is Overchannel-class by its own description, fires reactively, and is designed to be used repeatedly against a crowd. A working that fires many times per engagement and accumulates permanent fracture density each time is a different proposition from one that costs vertigo. The page's own honesty is what makes the gap conspicuous: it says an Overchannel-range release 'is not free simply because it started as someone else's hit', and then charges nothing that lasts.

options.option: State the Overchannel fracture accumulation as the working's real cost: each release deposits structural damage, with a stated count of releases before something becomes permanent.
options.changes: Gives the working a cost that constrains how often it is used and makes a long engagement genuinely expensive, which is the fairness answer; needs a number, and the system gives no formula for fracture density.

options.option: Remove the Overchannel framing and price the release as ordinary banked output, so the clause and its penalty do not apply.
options.changes: Removes the unpaid liability and the page's only numeric anchor at the same time, which pushes the magnitude question in SA-PHYS-REPRISAL-YIELD-VS-STAGGER toward an absolute figure instead.

options.option: Cap the working by Overchannel exposure rather than by capacity: a stated number of releases per engagement before Backlash lands.
options.changes: Answers this row and the page's own open question about a ceiling at once, with a mechanism the system already has; competes with Cinerion's Fouling, which the register offers as the more interesting ceiling.

options.option: Keep the cost as written and accept that this working's Overchannel use is exempt because the energy was the attacker's.
options.changes: Matches the page's instinct and its 'not free simply because it started as someone else's hit' line argues against it; creates a precedent that redirected force carries no Overchannel penalty, which every absorb-and-return working could claim.

quote_a: **Function** · Reads the target's current Essence state and casts it outward as a construct that carries the same signature and moves under its own limited agency, so anything tracking the target's Essence contour, sight-line, or predictive pattern spends its attention on the construct instead.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · Every element absorbs and emits at wavelengths fixed by its own electron structure, and no substance can present another's spectrum. Judicium tunes Gnosis to that principle: the practitioner reads the characteristic lines of a Crystal, a technique, or a lie, and identifies composition from signature alone. Eddy-current inspection finds the crack under the paint without removing the paint.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fulguria — Electromagnetism.md:22
why: The two workings bundled on this page stand on incompatible premises about whether a signature can be counterfeited. Speculum Harmoniae casts a target's Essence state outward 'as a construct that carries the same signature', and its whole function is that trackers keyed to that signature read the construct as the genuine article. Nexus Harmoniae, on the same page, is governed by Judicium, whose Mechanism states a uniqueness law in the strongest available terms: 'no substance can present another's spectrum', and whose identification works 'from signature alone'. Judicium is the system's instrument of identification precisely because signatures are held to be unforgeable. If an Essence signature is a spectroscopic quantity in the sense the register means, the Speculum cannot exist. If it is not, then Judicium's reading of 'a Crystal, a technique, or a lie' is a weaker instrument than its register claims, and every working in the corpus that identifies by signature inherits that weakness. The page takes neither reading and does not notice that it needs one. This is not a small inconsistency of flavour: Judicium's uniqueness clause is the reason signature identification is treated as reliable anywhere in the system.

options.option: Rule that an Essence signature is not a composition and carries no uniqueness law, so signature-matching constructs are legal and Judicium identifies by correlation rather than by law.
options.changes: Legalises the Speculum and every decoy working; weakens Judicium and every identification, alibi and forensic use built on it, including the Reprisal harness's threshold reading.

options.option: Rule that signature is unique by law, and rebuild the Speculum so the construct carries a *plausible* signature rather than the target's own.
options.changes: Preserves Judicium; costs the Speculum its stated Function and makes the counter a detection roll against plausibility rather than the clean channel-change the page has.

options.option: Split the quantity: composition is unique (Judicium's domain) and surface resonance contour is not (the Speculum's), and say so in the Core Vocabulary.
options.changes: Resolves both, and requires a new distinction in the vocabulary that several existing pages use interchangeably; also makes 'read the contour' and 'read the composition' different acts with different Sub-Stats.

options.option: Leave both and treat the Speculum as an exploit of Judicium's blind spot, stated on the page.
options.changes: Keeps every word and turns the contradiction into content, but requires the page to say which reading Judicium practitioners believe, and gives the Speculum an automatic counter in any Judicium user who knows the exploit.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Specular reflection, the same phase-conjugate law Mirithane runs on: what leaves the Shell returns the wavefront that was put into it, with no flattering correction. Serenyra takes a true reading of the target and lets the reading walk. Oneirion supplies the conceptual space the reading walks through, so the construct behaves like a body rather than an afterimage.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · A true mirror adds nothing. Angle in equals angle out, and fidelity is defined entirely by the absence of introduced distortion. A phase-conjugate mirror goes further and returns a wavefront that undoes its own aberration on the way back. Mirithane makes the Shell such a surface, so what leaves the practitioner is what was in them, with no flattering correction applied in transit.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:43
why: Optical phase conjugation is real, and its defining property is time reversal: the conjugate wave is the complex conjugate of the incoming one, so it retraces the incoming path backwards through whatever distorted it, which is exactly why it undoes aberration and why a phase-conjugate mirror returns a beam toward its source. That is a backward-propagating wave. Speculum Harmoniae needs a second forward-propagating source that walks away from the original and is seen by third parties from their own directions. The device that does that is a repeater or transponder: it receives a signature and re-radiates a new wave from a different place. A conjugate mirror cannot produce one, and the difference is not a detail - it is the direction of propagation. The register agrees with the physics and not with the page: Mirithane 'makes the Shell such a surface, so what leaves the practitioner is what was in them', which is a law about the practitioner's own emission leaving honestly, not about copying a third party outward. The page's substance (a faithful copy, no flattering correction) survives; its named law does not produce it.

options.option: Re-describe the Mechanism as a repeater: a faithful re-radiation of a received signature from a new position, with Mirithane supplying the fidelity rather than the geometry.
options.changes: Keeps every stated effect, the cost and the counter, and costs the page its phase-conjugation citation; makes the fidelity claim about the *copy* rather than about reflection.

options.option: Keep phase conjugation and restrict the working to what a conjugate mirror can do: return a pursuer's own read back at him, so he tracks his own reflected signature.
options.changes: Physically exact and a different working - no independent double, no limited agency, no three exchanges; loses the page's Effect entirely and gains a cleaner one.

options.option: Rule that Mirithane's law governs fidelity in general rather than reflection geometry, so the phase-conjugate clause of its Analogue is illustrative.
options.changes: Legalises this page and every other Mirithane working that copies outward; weakens the register's most precise clause, which other pages may be relying on.

quote_a: **Counter** · A working that reads the reversion's shape before it completes, or a sense keyed to fear, hatred, or grief rather than surface signature, tells the two bodies apart. *A hunter tracking emotion rather than Essence contour is not fooled.*
quote_b: > **Failure** · The mirror does not discriminate. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:45
why: The page's Counter requires that the double not carry affect: an emotional tracker keyed to fear, hatred or grief tells the two bodies apart because the copy reproduces only 'surface signature'. The page's Mechanism requires the opposite quality - a true reading with 'no flattering correction' - and Mirithane's register states the consequence as a Failure that does not admit exceptions: 'The mirror does not discriminate. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly.' The page's leading use is Serenyra mirroring herself while pursued ('A pursuer chasing Serenyra'), which is exactly the case the Failure describes, and the state she is in while being hunted is exactly the channel the Counter relies on being absent. So either the mirror is honest, in which case the affect is copied and the page's only channel-orthogonal counter fails against its primary use; or the copy is a surface read that omits interior state, in which case it is not a Mirithane mirror in the register's sense and the fidelity claim is decoration. The physics is indifferent between these - decoy rejection needs a channel in which the two differ, and which channels those are is a canon decision - but the page needs one of them and states both.

options.option: Rule the copy surface-only: it carries what she read from outside and nothing interior, so the emotional counter holds and the Mechanism's fidelity claim is narrowed to the read.
options.changes: Keeps the counter, which is the fairest thing on the page; costs the Mechanism its 'no flattering correction' framing and puts the Speculum outside Mirithane's stated law.

options.option: Rule the copy honest, including affect, and replace the Counter with a different orthogonal channel (mass, kinematics, the projection error Oneirion's Failure predicts).
options.changes: Keeps the register intact and makes the working stronger against emotional trackers; the replacement counters already exist in the page (touch, no mass) and in Oneirion's Failure, so nothing becomes uncounterable.

options.option: Split by target: mirroring herself copies affect (Mirithane's law on her own Shell), mirroring a third party copies only what she read.
options.changes: Resolves both quotes and makes the working's counter depend on whose double it is, which is interesting and adds a rule a player must look up to use.

quote_a: **Sub-Stats** · Dominion Sovereignty, Gnosis Acuity, Gnosis Analysis, Harmonics Attunement.
quote_b: **Path** · **Spirit dominant, Fate secondary.** *The card's own progression is Spirit → Mind → Fate; Mind is struck as Choir vocabulary and not one of the four, and the stated destination, Fate, is committed as her secondary — memory and emotional signature used to forecast the state of Wellsprings.* **The Fate Path routes no force here; it is a reading, not a weapon, and nothing on this sheet needs it to be more.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:73
why: Both workings on this page list Harmonics Attunement, whose gate is 'Attunement requires Attraction Path at Stage II to exceed D' (Part Seven, Harmonics Gates). Speculum Harmoniae requires B-Grade and Nexus Harmoniae S-Grade; both exceed D, so the Attraction gate binds on both. Serenyra's card denies her Attraction at any weight: 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary', with the note that even the Fate Path 'routes no force here'. The hole is not one gate. Nexus Harmoniae's allied half is Harmonics Synergy verbatim ('allies hit harder standing near you'), whose gate is 'Synergy requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed S for ambient amplification and Stage VI to exceed A for allied amplification' - S exceeds A. Its kilometre envelope is a Dominion Radius, whose gate is 'Radius requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A', and her Dominion is 496, S-Grade. And the category itself demands it: Concordia is the 'Spirit-Attraction Apex' and says why - 'Attraction-side reach to hold that alignment as a lasting Domain rather than a passing chord'. Her card's own listed Category Harmonia is 'Spirit <-> Attraction' as well. This is the third of her pages to fail on the same missing Path after SA-CROSS-SOMNIUM-SERENYRA-PATH, which makes it a decision about the card rather than about any one technique.

options.option: Add Attraction to her card at the weight the gates need (Stage VI to exceed A).
options.changes: Legalises three of her pages at once and two of her four listed Categories; contradicts the card's own characterisation, which argues at length that she is a reader and not a projector.

options.option: Rebuild both workings on Spirit- and Fate-gated Sub-Stats only, dropping Attunement and the Synergy/Radius functions.
options.changes: Keeps the card; costs the Nexus its allied-amplification half and its kilometre radius, which is most of what it is, and costs the Speculum the Sub-Stat it inherited from Mirithane.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring harmonisation supplies the Path commitment for Sub-Stats that Wellspring strengthens, so Mirithane's Fidelity carries Attunement without Attraction.
options.changes: Resolves this row and a class of others across the batch; a large change to Part Seven's meaning, since Part Seven says commitment 'is not declared. It is recognized by the Crystal based on behavioral pattern'.

options.option: Reassign both workings to another practitioner who carries Attraction, and keep Serenyra as the author rather than the user.
options.changes: Keeps card and pages intact and needs a name the corpus does not currently supply for either working; also strands the Speculum's cost, which is written around her memory.

quote_a: **Sub-Stats** · Gnosis Cognition, Harmonics Attunement, Dominion Sovereignty.
quote_b: **Retention** — Clarity and accessibility of the Crystalline Memory structure under pressure, and the number of complete working structures held loaded in active cognitive memory without external inscription. *Absorbs Memorium.*
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:54
why: The page's three Sub-Stats are each what one of its Wellsprings strengthens - Cognition and Sovereignty (Reach) off Oneirion, Attunement (Fidelity) off Mirithane - and none of them is what the working does. The stated Cost is a memory debit: 'Every mirror spends a slice of her own sensory record of the target ... the read is thinner until she rebuilds it by observing them again.' That is Gnosis Retention, 'Clarity and accessibility of the Crystalline Memory structure under pressure', absorbing Memorium. The stated Limit is a construct-solidity statement: 'The double cannot land a real blow. Struck once by anything that matters, it stops existing.' That is Ardency Density, 'Structural weight and coherence of anything a working leaves standing ... whether your summon is a suggestion or a participant'. Neither is listed. Worse, the one Gnosis Sub-Stat the page does list is defined as the stat that defeats this working: Cognition is 'resistance to glamours, false spatial constructs and psychic misdirection'. So the page's component list contains the counter-stat and omits both stats that carry its cost and its limit. The same shape was logged on Sovereign's Reprisal as SA-CROSS-REPRISAL-FORTIFICATION-MISSING: a page deriving Sub-Stats from what its Wellsprings strengthen rather than from what the working does.

options.option: Add Gnosis Retention and Ardency Density to the FOW line and keep Cognition as the Wellspring-derived third.
options.changes: Makes cost and limit mechanical; Ardency Density's gate is 'Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B' (Part Seven), which Serenyra does not carry, so it may push the working to B-Grade or below or add to SA-CROSS-SPECULUM-ATTRACTION-PATH.

options.option: Add Retention only, and leave the double's fragility as a stated Limit rather than a Sub-Stat outcome.
options.changes: Cheapest fix and prices the cost correctly; leaves 'struck once it stops existing' unmodelled, so nothing in the system says whether a stronger practitioner's double survives a hit.

options.option: Remove Cognition, on the grounds that the resisting stat should not be a component of the working it resists.
options.changes: Tidies the list and loses the page's only Oneirion-derived Gnosis entry; Cognition's other clause (engaging higher-dimensional constructs without fragmentation) is arguably what lets her hold the manifold read, so the removal needs an argument.

options.option: Leave the list as the Wellspring derivation and state in the Codex line that Sub-Stats are derived from harmonisation rather than function.
options.changes: Consistent with several pages in this batch and makes the derivation a rule instead of an oversight; means no page's Sub-Stat list can be read as a description of what the working does.

quote_a: **Category** · Animatria, a detached fragment of her Essence Core given brief independent operation and motion, which is why it fails outright against anything that severs the live line back to her.
quote_b: **Categories** · **Glyphica, Harmonia, Domain Weaving, Mnemata.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:42
why: The page files Speculum Harmoniae under Animatria and reasons from the category correctly, quoting its continuity requirement almost exactly as the taxonomy states it. Serenyra's card lists her Categories as 'Glyphica, Harmonia, Domain Weaving, Mnemata' - four, and Animatria is not among them. The card's Mnemata covers the working's memory cost and Harmonia covers the Nexus half, so the omission is specifically the construct-projection category, which is the one the Speculum is built on. Nothing in the system says whether a card's Categories line is an exhaustive statement of what a practitioner can do or a summary of what she is known for, and that is the real question this row asks: several pages in this batch assign a Category that the practitioner's card does not list, and the answer decides whether those are errors or ordinary reach. Animatria's Path alignment does not add to the problem - it is 'Spirit-Aligned' and she is Spirit dominant - so this is a bookkeeping question rather than a gate failure.

options.option: Add Animatria to her card's Categories line.
options.changes: Smallest change; makes her a projector of constructs, which the card's Path note argues against in spirit if not in gates.

options.option: Rule that a card's Categories line is indicative rather than exhaustive, and say so in the schema.
options.changes: Clears this row and every other page in the batch with the same shape at once; removes the Categories line's usefulness as a check.

options.option: Re-file the Speculum under a Category her card carries - Mnemata for the read, Glyphica for the traced circle.
options.changes: Keeps the card and costs the page its best-reasoned paragraph, since the Animatria continuity clause is where the working's whole failure mode comes from.

quote_a: | **Limina** | **Spirit** primary · **Medium** at Veil-Thin density and above | Darkness, silence, Aether-thin ground, ruins | Saturated Aether, crowd density, active Domains |
path_a: wiki/The Magic System/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings.md:154
quote_b: **The Lattice of Living Light (Prototype)** · *Current Domain, nascent and portable.* **Focused on spatial law and harmonic perfection; every Aether thread within it is legible, a spell-tapestry and an archive at once.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:99
why: The Environmental Coupling table lists 'active Domains' among Limina's suppressive conditions, alongside saturated Aether and crowd density, and the page that carries the table insists the effect is mechanical rather than decorative: 'Terrain is not flavour. It is a modifier on eta.' It does not say whose Domains. Serenyra holds one - the Lattice of Living Light, 'Current Domain, nascent and portable' - and Speculum Harmoniae is a Limina working. If the table means any active Domain, then she suppresses her own Limina workings whenever her Domain is up, and since Nexus Harmoniae is a field of the same size and shape on the same page, the two halves of this page cannot be used together. If it means an opponent's only, the row needs to say so, because a portable Domain follows its holder everywhere and the reading decides whether every Domain-holding Limina practitioner in the corpus is permanently self-suppressed. The same ambiguity reaches Aeldoris Vanthryx and every other Limina page in the batch, which is why this is filed as a gap in the table rather than a fault on this page. Note the crowd-density clause has the same flavour of problem and is not ambiguous, only ironic: a decoy is worth most in a press of bodies and the press suppresses the Family it is built from.

options.option: Rule that 'active Domains' means Domains other than the practitioner's own.
options.changes: Clears every Limina practitioner who holds a Domain, which is most of them above Stage VIII; leaves Domain-dense engagements as a real Limina problem, which is the interesting half.

options.option: Rule that it means any active Domain, including the practitioner's own, and accept the self-suppression.
options.changes: Makes the two workings on this page mutually exclusive and gives every Limina practitioner a reason not to raise their Domain, which is a large and findable tactical rule.

options.option: Replace 'active Domains' with a stated density or count, so the suppression scales rather than switching.
options.changes: Needs a number the system does not have, and Aetheric Density has no numeric scale to hang it on (SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY).

quote_a: **Target Response** · Allied workings read as marginally stronger and enemy workings as marginally weaker for as long as they pass through the field; every working in range becomes slightly more predictable to anyone reading the field itself.
quote_b: **Synergy** — The degree to which ambient Wellspring activity feeds the character's Harmonic state and the Harmonic field synchronises with and amplifies allied resonances. You fight stronger near active veins and allies hit harder standing near you. *Absorbs Confluence.*
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:81
why: Nexus Harmoniae does two symmetrical things: allied workings read stronger and enemy workings read weaker. Only one half has a Sub-Stat. Harmonics Synergy is the allied half verbatim - 'the Harmonic field synchronises with and amplifies allied resonances ... allies hit harder standing near you' - and it covers ambient and allied amplification and nothing else. The obvious candidate for the other half is Harmonics Suppression, and it is not that: 'Consciously compressing or masking the resonance field to reduce detectability and conceal Temperance tier. The volume knob on the soul' - self-concealment, not attenuation of somebody else's working. Nothing among the sixty-four weakens another practitioner's working in transit. Dominion Pressure and Sovereignty act on geometry and law inside a Domain, not on a third party's output; Gnosis Analysis reads. The physics says the same thing from the other side: a field can give coherent gain to what shares its phase reference and incoherent gain to what does not, which is an *absence* of amplification rather than a suppression, so the two halves of the stated effect are not mirror images and only one of them is a thing a field does. Either the enemy half needs a Sub-Stat the system does not have, or it is the allied half seen from outside and should be described that way.

options.option: Re-describe the effect as amplification only: allies gain, enemies are simply not gaining, which is what the coherent-summation mechanism actually produces.
options.changes: Needs no new Sub-Stat, closes the physics, and halves the page's stated effect; relative advantage is unchanged, so the working is as strong and less symmetrical.

options.option: Add a Harmonics Sub-Stat for attenuating a third party's working in transit.
options.changes: Adds a sixty-fifth Sub-Stat to a list the system deliberately consolidated from one hundred and twenty to sixty-four, and would need a gate and a ladder.

options.option: Route the enemy half through Dominion Pressure and declare the Nexus a Domain, so the debuff is a Domain Expression rather than a Harmonics effect.
options.changes: Uses machinery that exists and makes the Nexus a Domain, which brings Domain costs, the Domain-versus-Domain hierarchy and the collapse shockwave with it (SA-CROSS-NEXUS-DOMAIN-OR-WORKING, SA-FAIR-NEXUS-COLLAPSE-SHOCKWAVE).

quote_a: **Function** · Raises a wide, faint field over an area; any working cast or already active inside it is routed through the field before its outcome resolves, which is where Serenyra applies her bias.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:100
why: The Nexus is centrally arbitrated - she applies the bias, and every biased working must therefore complete a round trip from wherever it was cast to her and back before it resolves. Two floors apply and neither is in the page. The channel floor is light: a kilometre is 3.3 microseconds one way, so 6.7 microseconds round trip at the rim, which is fast. The practitioner floor is Part Six: S-Grade Reaction Speed is 0.05-0.2 ms, that is 50-200 microseconds, so she is the bottleneck by a factor of seven to thirty and the physical channel is never the constraint. That means any working which resolves faster than her reaction window cannot be routed at all, and Part Six names what does: S-Grade Attack Speed is Mach 50-500, and at Mach 500 (about 170 km/s) a strike crosses Part Eleven's S-Grade Contact Range of 5-15 m in 30-90 microseconds - inside her floor. An SS-Grade opponent, whose reaction is stated as 'below 0.05 ms', is outside her arbitration entirely, and Part Six adds that at SS 'biological neural processes are insufficient'. The working is therefore bounded to slower exchanges and to distance, and this is a counter a player can derive from two tables. Nothing here says the Nexus is wrong; it says the Nexus has an unstated limit that happens to be its best counterplay route.

options.option: State the limit on the page: the Nexus cannot bias a working that resolves faster than her Reaction Speed, and name the Grade at which that begins.
options.changes: Costs nothing, adds a findable counter, and makes the working's value scale with the pace of the fight rather than with its size.

options.option: Make the bias local rather than centrally arbitrated: the field carries a standing rule she set in advance, applied where the working is, with no round trip.
options.changes: Removes the latency floor entirely and removes 'which is where Serenyra applies her bias', so she cannot respond to individual workings; makes the Nexus a set-and-hold field and a different tool.

options.option: Keep central arbitration and accept that fast close exchanges pass unbiased, without stating it.
options.changes: Leaves the derivation available to anyone who reads Part Six and Part Eleven, which is the challenge working as intended, and leaves the page claiming 'any working cast or already active inside it' when the arithmetic says otherwise.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Judicium's discernment law reads each working's tonal structure the way a Thaumic Harmonist reads a spell in progress; Aurevane's illumination law carries that reading across the whole field at once rather than letting it fade with distance, which is what makes the effect battlefield-scale instead of line-of-sight.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · Two points are resolvable only when their diffraction patterns separate, and coherent light holds a fixed phase relationship across its whole front, which is what makes a laser a laser rather than a bright lamp. Aurevane raises both figures at once. What the practitioner perceives resolves finer, and what they express leaves the Shell in phase, meaning the output matches the intent with almost no distortion introduced in transit.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fulguria — Electromagnetism.md:29
why: The page uses Aurevane to defeat distance: its 'illumination law carries that reading across the whole field at once rather than letting it fade with distance, which is what makes the effect battlefield-scale instead of line-of-sight'. Aurevane's register does not say that and the physics it names does not do that. The Analogue is 'Optical resolution and coherence. The Rayleigh criterion; phase-locked emission', and the Mechanism is about resolution and phase: 'coherent light holds a fixed phase relationship across its whole front, which is what makes a laser a laser rather than a bright lamp'. Coherence preserves phase, not amplitude. A laser still spreads and its intensity still falls with distance; what it does not lose is the phase relationship across its front. So Aurevane supplies exactly the thing the Nexus's mechanism needs - a common phase reference across a kilometre, which is what lets correlated workings sum coherently and uncorrelated ones incoherently - and supplies nothing at all against falloff. The consequence is that the bias cannot be uniform: it must be strongest at her position and weakest at the rim, on any inverse-power law. The page states a flat envelope ('Radius up to roughly one kilometre'), and the correct reading hands an opponent a free counter, which is to stand near the edge.

options.option: State the bias as falling with distance from her, with the kilometre as the range at which it becomes negligible rather than the range at which it stops.
options.changes: Matches the physics and Part Eleven's own convention for Projected Force Range, which is defined at fifty percent yield; adds a gradient a player can exploit and costs the page nothing it needs.

options.option: Keep the flat envelope and re-attribute the non-falloff to something other than Aurevane - a Domain boundary, which does have a stated edge.
options.changes: Preserves the effect and makes the Nexus a Domain, pulling in SA-CROSS-NEXUS-DOMAIN-OR-WORKING and the Domain cost and collapse rules.

options.option: Correct the Mechanism to use Aurevane for the phase reference only, and let the field's reach come from the radius rather than from the law.
options.changes: Most accurate to both the register and the mechanism; leaves unstated what actually sets the radius, which is currently Dominion Radius and gated on a Path she lacks.

quote_a: **Counter** · A strong personal Domain partially insulates its owner from the nexus's bias, and a Wellspring technique built to mute its own signature ducks under her detection entirely.
quote_b: **The Lattice of Living Light (Prototype)** · *Current Domain, nascent and portable.* **Focused on spatial law and harmonic perfection; every Aether thread within it is legible, a spell-tapestry and an archive at once.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:99
why: The capability the Nexus describes is already on Serenyra's card as her Domain. The Lattice of Living Light is 'Focused on spatial law and harmonic perfection; every Aether thread within it is legible, a spell-tapestry and an archive at once', and the card repeats it as her Attraction Layer. Reading every working inside a field is what the Nexus does. The page instead presents the Nexus as a Spellcraft working, chanted and gestured through a staff, with a stated radius and duration. The distinction is not cosmetic, because the system rules Domains and does not rule fields. If the Nexus is her Domain, Part Twenty-Two applies: maintenance costs Essence continuously and scales with Dominion Radius; the Domain-versus-Domain hierarchy governs the page's own stated counter; and collapse produces a Resonance Shockwave. And the hierarchy contradicts the page directly: the page says a strong personal Domain 'partially insulates its owner', while Part Twenty-Two gives no partial outcome - 'A character two or more Stages above their opponent's Domain simply overwrites it', and within a band 'the character with higher Sovereignty and Gravity holds their territory while the weaker Domain erodes'. If the Nexus is not a Domain, then the system has no rule at all for a Domain overlapping a non-Domain field, and the page's counter is unadjudicable.

options.option: Declare the Nexus an expression of the Lattice of Living Light rather than a separate working, and apply Part Twenty-Two throughout.
options.changes: Unifies card and page, supplies the maintenance cost the page lacks, replaces 'partially insulates' with the four-step hierarchy, and brings the collapse shockwave (SA-FAIR-NEXUS-COLLAPSE-SHOCKWAVE).

options.option: Keep the Nexus a working and rewrite its Counter in terms the system can adjudicate, without invoking Domains.
options.changes: Keeps card and page separate and duplicates the Lattice's reading function in two places; needs a new rule for what beats a field, since the register's routes assume Domain, ward or anchor.

options.option: Write the missing rule: how a Domain interacts with a non-Domain field of Concordia class.
options.changes: Fills a real hole that other pages will need; a new general rule, which is a larger change than this page.

options.option: Rule that 'partially insulates' is the intended outcome and that Part Twenty-Two's hierarchy applies only Domain against Domain.
options.changes: Keeps the page's wording; creates a class of fields against which a Domain is only partly effective, which several Domain-holders in the corpus would want to test.

quote_a: **Limit** · The bias is small. It is a strategist's tool, not a battlefield-ending one, and it drops the instant she loses consciousness or leaves the field.
quote_b: A Domain collapses when EU drops below the minimum maintenance threshold, when concentration is shattered by sufficient force, or when a stronger Domain overwrites it. Collapse produces a **Resonance Shockwave** proportional to the Domain's size and density, often dealing significant damage to everything within the former territory, including the character who lost it.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VIII. Traits, Soul Crystal Tiers, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two).md:122
why: The Nexus's failure costs nothing. It 'drops the instant she loses consciousness or leaves the field', and that is the whole of it - a kilometre-wide field switching off cleanly. The system prices the same event very differently for a Domain: 'Collapse produces a Resonance Shockwave proportional to the Domain's size and density, often dealing significant damage to everything within the former territory, including the character who lost it.' A kilometre is the largest radius in the batch, and the card already calls this capability her Domain (SA-CROSS-NEXUS-DOMAIN-OR-WORKING). Two things follow. First, the working fails the cost test in the direction that matters: a practitioner who can raise a battlefield-scale field with no penalty for losing it has been handed the upside of a Domain without its liability, and the register's own reading of costs applies - 'Waiting for the cost' does not work as a counter because there is no cost to wait for. Second, the page has thrown away its best beat. A field that kills everything inside it when its holder goes down makes her allies' interest in protecting her physical rather than sentimental, and makes an opponent's decision to drop her a decision about a kilometre of his own men too. The page's sustain cost is well judged; it is the termination that is free.

options.option: Apply the Resonance Shockwave on collapse, scaled to the stated radius, and say so in the Limit line.
options.changes: Prices the working honestly and makes both sides' tactics turn on her body; needs a magnitude, and 'proportional to size and density' supplies no number (SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA, SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY).

options.option: Keep the clean drop and justify it: a Concordia alignment released rather than broken, with an explicit distinction between a released field and a shattered one.
options.changes: Preserves the page and needs the distinction written into Part Twenty-Two, since 'concentration is shattered by sufficient force' is exactly what losing consciousness is.

options.option: Charge the collapse to her alone - backlash on the holder, nothing on the field.
options.changes: Adds a cost that hurts without making her allies hostages; loses the tactical texture and is a smaller change than the register implies.

options.option: Cap the radius so that a collapse at that scale is survivable, and let the shockwave apply.
options.changes: Resolves the fairness question by shrinking the working; the 1 km figure is currently the page's one exactly-in-band number, matching the S-Grade Passive Pressure Field row.

quote_a: **Craft** · Spellcraft, spoken and gestured (a chant with a sweeping gesture, carried through the Aether Chord Staff, unattested item in current canon, kept as her named focus).
quote_b: **Aether Chord Staff** · *Focusing implement.* **Magnifies her tones and extends the range of her lattices to 10 km.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:98
why: CORRECTED 2026-09-25. The row as first filed said 'Her card lists no equipment entry for it, and nothing else in the corpus names it.' Both halves are wrong and the second is checkable in one search. Serenyra's card carries the Staff under Artifacts: 'Aether Chord Staff - Focusing implement. Magnifies her tones and extends the range of her lattices to 10 km.' It is also named on Edictum Resonantiae, on Speculum Harmoniae and on Symphonia Ascendant. The item is attested. What remains, and is the real conflict, is narrower and still worth a ruling: the Nexus Harmoniae page declares the Staff 'unattested item in current canon' when it is not, and separately makes the Staff the carrier of a working performed by a practitioner whose Stage exempts her from needing a carrier. Law V: 'At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all.' Serenyra is Stage VIII. So the Staff is a choice, and a choice that hands an opponent Counterplay's 'Interrupt the chain' against a working that should be immune to it. The card gives the Staff a range figure (10 km) and the technique pages state shorter ranges, so what the Staff actually contributes - reach, amplitude, or nothing the practitioner could not do unaided - is the open question.

options.option: Strike the 'unattested item in current canon' clause from the Nexus page, since the card and three technique pages name the Staff.
options.changes: A factual correction and nothing more; leaves the load-bearing question (what the Staff contributes to a working whose practitioner needs no anchor) open.

options.option: State what the Staff does mechanically - the card says it magnifies her tones and carries her lattices to 10 km - and price each working's reach against that figure.
options.changes: Makes the Staff checkable and makes taking it a real counter with a stated effect; requires reconciling the 10 km with the shorter ranges the technique pages state (Symphonia 5 km, Somnium 200 m).

options.option: Rule that an above-Refraction practitioner using a focus is choosing amplitude over invulnerability to chain-interruption, and say so on the pages that use one.
options.changes: Turns a filing inconsistency into a stated trade-off available to players; would apply to every above-Refraction practitioner in the corpus who carries a focus.

options.option: Remove the Staff from the Nexus's Craft line so the working is held internally as her Stage allows.
options.changes: Closes the interrupt route and costs the page its most concrete image; the Staff would remain on the card and on the other three pages.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · This runs on real destructive-interference logic: two waveforms of matched frequency and opposed phase cancel where a matched, in-phase pair would reinforce. The Thesauriel imprints the incoming working's frequency signature closely enough to build a phase-inverted double, and the collision is where the two workings would otherwise have completed themselves.
quote_b: > **What nobody knows.** Why the echo comes back fractured and dissonant rather than a clean copy of the original, when every other part of the recording is exact.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Speculum Recordatio.md:21
why: The page names destructive interference as its mechanism and states the law correctly, including the reinforcing case: 'two waveforms of matched frequency and opposed phase cancel where a matched, in-phase pair would reinforce.' It then treats only the cancelling branch as an outcome. Superposition does not work that way. With an anti-wave of matched amplitude and phase error theta from perfect inversion, the residual is 2A*|sin(theta/2)|, which gives: theta = 5.7 degrees, 20 dB of cancellation (this is the working tolerance of real active noise control, where 20 dB needs amplitude match within 1 dB and phase within 6 degrees and disturbance-to-anti-signal correlation above 0.995); theta = 60 degrees, output equal to the original, nothing achieved; theta = 120 degrees, output 1.73A, +4.8 dB, the incoming working made stronger. So the working has an unstated sign change at sixty degrees, above which it amplifies what it was cast to stop. And the phase error is not free to choose, because theta = 2*pi*f*delta_t with delta_t her own processing latency: at the A-Grade Reaction Speed of 0.2-1 ms (Part Six) the 6-degree tolerance holds only to 16-80 Hz and the sign change arrives at 167-833 Hz. This also answers the page's own 'What nobody knows': the echo is fractured because what returns is the residual - low frequencies subtracted, high frequencies doubled at scrambled phase - and an exact record does not buy an exact inverse, because an inverse must be timed as well as shaped. Nothing here is a contradiction between two canon texts; it is a regime the page has not stated, and it is simultaneously the working's best counter and the answer to its own open question.

options.option: State the reinforcement regime on the page as a failure mode, with the frequency or speed threshold expressed through Part Six's Reaction Speed ladder.
options.changes: Gives the working a fourth failure mode that is dramatic and self-inflicted, and hands opponents a counter that costs only pace; requires the page to accept that a counter-working can help an attack.

options.option: Answer the 'What nobody knows' line on the page with the residual explanation and leave the sign change implicit.
options.changes: Closes the page's open question with its own mechanism and keeps the derivation available to any player who does the arithmetic; leaves the page claiming three outcomes where there are four.

options.option: Rule that the Thesauriel's imprint includes timing, so phase error is bounded by the recording rather than by her reaction speed.
options.changes: Removes the frequency ceiling and the reinforcement regime and makes the working much stronger; also removes the physical explanation for the fracture, which would then need a new cause.

options.option: Keep the page as written and treat 'fractured and dissonant' as unexplained flavour.
options.changes: No edits; leaves a derivable regime in which the working assists the attacker undocumented, which is the one outcome a player would most want warned about.

quote_a: **Counterplay** · Attack faster than the imprint completes, or attack with a casting whose scale is calibrated to exceed what a single Thesauriel reading can hold.
quote_b: **Cost** · One memory slot per use, and a paroxysmal Aether surge that leaves her mentally addled for a moment afterward.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Speculum Recordatio.md:37
why: The page states no tell. Its Counterplay line tells an opponent to 'Attack faster than the imprint completes' without saying how he would know an imprint is being taken, which makes the stated counter unusable by anyone who has not read the technique page - the exact failure the fair-play brief is written against. The material is already in the page's own lines. The Craft is Runecraft through an instrument, and the card calls that instrument 'Runecraft in a book', so the working requires a codex raised and held open before the incoming working lands. The imprint takes time she must be seen to spend, since the page's own Counter turns on a caster finishing before it completes. And the Cost leaves her 'mentally addled for a moment afterward' with 'a blank space in her recent memory', which is a visible window immediately after every use. Three tells, all stated as other things, none stated as a tell. This is a fairness failure of omission rather than of design: nothing needs weakening, the page needs a sentence.

options.option: State the tell as the raised codex and the visible imprint interval, and the window as the addled moment after.
options.changes: Makes both stated counters usable at the table and costs the working nothing; the imprint interval becomes a quantity someone will ask for a number for.

options.option: State only the aftermath as the tell, leaving the imprint itself silent.
options.changes: Keeps the working hard to pre-empt and gives an opponent a reliable read after the first use; the 'attack faster' counter stays unusable on the first exchange.

options.option: Rule the working has no tell by design and remove 'attack faster than the imprint completes' from the Counterplay line.
options.changes: Internally consistent and removes the working's cheapest counter, leaving only scale; makes a Runecraft counter-working that announces nothing, which the Craft's own substrate arguably forbids.

quote_a: **Cost** · One memory slot per use, and a paroxysmal Aether surge that leaves her mentally addled for a moment afterward.
quote_b: **Retention** — Clarity and accessibility of the Crystalline Memory structure under pressure, and the number of complete working structures held loaded in active cognitive memory without external inscription. *Absorbs Memorium.*
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md:54
why: The page charges its cost in a unit the system already defines and then lists neither the unit nor its Sub-Stat. 'One memory slot per use' is Gnosis Retention's own measure: Retention is 'Clarity and accessibility of the Crystalline Memory structure under pressure, and the number of complete working structures held loaded in active cognitive memory without external inscription'. A memory slot holding a complete working structure is exactly what Retention counts. The page's FOW line instead gives 'Governing Primary Gnosis (Diagnosis, Perception) and Harmonics (Fidelity)', which under the Merge Ledger is Analysis, Perception and Attunement - the three Sub-Stats its two Wellspring registers strengthen, and nothing the working costs. So the working's resource has no stat behind it: nothing says how many slots a practitioner has, whether a spent slot returns, or what Retention Grade buys. This is the second consecutive Serenyra page to charge a Retention cost without naming Retention (SA-CROSS-SPECULUM-RETENTION-DENSITY), and the third instance in the batch of a page deriving its Sub-Stats from what its Wellsprings strengthen rather than from what the working does (SA-CROSS-REPRISAL-FORTIFICATION-MISSING).

options.option: Add Gnosis Retention to the FOW line and price the cost against its Grade, so a higher Retention means more slots or faster recovery.
options.changes: Gives the cost a mechanism and a scaling; needs a slot count per Grade, which the system does not supply, and Retention's own gate is Spirit-Path at Stage II to exceed D, which she passes.

options.option: Keep the FOW line and re-describe the cost in EU or in a stated recovery time rather than in slots.
options.changes: Removes the unmodelled unit; loses the page's best feature, since a countable memory debt is a more interesting cost than a reserve drain and is the only one of its kind in the batch.

options.option: Rule that 'memory slot' is shorthand for Retention capacity generally and needs no separate entry.
options.changes: Smallest change and leaves every question about how many, how long and what recovers unanswered on every page that uses the phrase.

quote_a: **Counter** · A caster who finishes an effect instantaneously, before the Thesauriel completes its imprint, is never caught by it; a Cataclysmic-tier casting overloads the recording and shatters the counterspell instead of catching it.
quote_b: | **T8** | Cataclysmic Entity | Hydra · Voidwyrm · Cerberus |
path_b: wiki/Bestiary/The Bestiary.md:45
why: The page prices its overload threshold with two terms that are not system vocabulary for workings. 'A Cataclysmic-tier casting' implies a tier ladder that includes Cataclysmic; the Tier Grade ladder runs F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS, X, EX, EX+, and 'Cataclysmic Entity' is T8 on the Bestiary's threat register, which classifies creatures - Hydra, Voidwyrm, Cerberus - rather than castings. Borrowing a creature threat tier to size a spell leaves the threshold uncheckable: nothing states what Tier Grade a T8 entity casts at, and the Bestiary ladder and the Grade ladder have no stated conversion. 'A-Temporal Void effects', in the Limit line, appears nowhere else in the corpus in any form. Both terms are load-bearing: the first sets where the recording breaks and the second sets what the working cannot touch at all. The page's other overload clause is well formed by contrast - 'a working two or more Tiers above her own ceiling' uses the Grade ladder and reads against Part Four's rule that one full Tier Grade above an opponent wins a direct exchange without meaningful contest.

options.option: Restate both thresholds in Tier Grades: name the Grade at which the recording overloads and the effect class that carries no signature.
options.changes: Makes both limits checkable against Part Four and Part Eleven; requires deciding what 'A-Temporal Void' was reaching for, which is probably Limina's Nihiloth or Dissolution kinds, already attested.
