options.option: Write a stated conversion between the Bestiary's threat tiers and the Tier Grade ladder.
options.changes: Fixes this page and a class of others that mix the two ladders; a large new rule, and the Bestiary's T3-T8 'Variable' row for Elementals shows the two do not map cleanly.

options.option: Keep 'Cataclysmic-tier' as in-world soldier's vocabulary and gloss it on the page with its Grade equivalent.
options.changes: Preserves the register's voice and makes the mechanic legible; needs the equivalence stated once.

options.option: Leave both terms and accept that the overload threshold and the immune class are narrative rather than mechanical.
options.changes: No edits; leaves the working's two hardest limits unadjudicable at the table, which is where a counter-working most needs to be adjudicable.

page: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md
quote_a: **Categories** · **Glyphica, Harmonia, Domain Weaving, Mnemata.**
path_a: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:42
quote_b: Sits between Spirit and Attraction because memory itself is Soul Plane, but its *transmission* between souls, generations, or into Domains is Attraction Force at work. The House of the Veil's Wellsprings (Anamnesis, Phreatis, Somnalis) are its most natural partners.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:188
why: The question the technique pages keep failing on lives on the card. Serenyra's Categories line lists four: Glyphica, Harmonia, Domain Weaving, Mnemata. The taxonomy aligns them as Glyphica 'Spirit-Aligned', Harmonia 'Spirit <-> Attraction', Mnemata 'Spirit <-> Attraction', Domain Weaving 'Attraction-Aligned'. Three of her four require Attraction on the taxonomy's own labels, one of them exclusively, and Mnemata says why in terms: memory is Soul Plane but 'its transmission between souls, generations, or into Domains is Attraction Force at work'. Her Path line denies her Attraction at any weight - 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary', with 'The Fate Path routes no force here'. Four of her technique pages then fail Attraction-gated Sub-Stats (SA-CROSS-SOMNIUM-SERENYRA-PATH, SA-CROSS-SPECULUM-ATTRACTION-PATH), and this row records why they all fail the same way. The prior question underneath it is whether a Category's alignment label is a Path requirement at all. Concordia states that it is, for itself - 'it requires both: Spirit-side precision ... and Attraction-side reach' - and no general rule says whether every alignment label carries the same force. Recorded, not resolved: the answer decides a character's sheet and a rule about what an alignment label means, which is more than one ruling.

options.option: Add Attraction to her Path line at the weight her Categories and Sub-Stat gates need.
options.changes: Clears three Categories and four technique pages in one move; contradicts the card's own argument that she is a reader rather than a projector, which is written as characterisation.

options.option: Rule that Category alignment labels are descriptive of where a practice sits in the taxonomy and impose no Path requirement, with Concordia's explicit clause the exception.
options.changes: Clears the Categories question across every card in the corpus and leaves the Part Seven Sub-Stat gates untouched, so the four technique pages still fail on Attunement, Synergy and Radius.

options.option: Narrow her Categories line to the ones her Path supports, dropping Domain Weaving and Mnemata.
options.changes: Keeps the Path line and costs her the Domain she is defined by and the memory practice three of her techniques are built on; almost certainly wrong, and stated here so the ruling can say so.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring harmonisation can supply the Attraction side of a Category or a Sub-Stat gate without a Path commitment.
options.changes: Resolves the card and every technique page at once; a large change to Part Seven, which says Path commitment 'is not declared. It is recognized by the Crystal based on behavioral pattern'.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Transmutatio's law is change of basis: a coordinate transformation under conservation, where nothing is created or destroyed and a quantity is only re-expressed in a more useful form. Applied to a living skeleton, it re-lattices existing bone and muscle into a denser, higher-output configuration, the same substance differently arranged. Ascensio's law is mechanical advantage, the path-independence of work done against a load: the same total transformation can be made without exceeding what the structure can bear, provided the stress is spread across a longer path instead of taken as one peak. Ascensio spreads the re-lattice's stress across the whole duration of the buff, so the skeleton never takes the full transformation cost in one instant.
quote_b: **Analogue** · Mechanical advantage. Path-independence of gravitational potential energy.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md:35
why: The page generalises a conservative-field theorem onto a dissipative process, and the register it cites is careful where the page is not. Ascensio's Analogue is 'Mechanical advantage. Path-independence of gravitational potential energy' - path-independence holds for conservative forces and for nothing else. The page restates it as 'the path-independence of work done against a load', dropping the qualifier, and then applies it to the plastic re-latticing of living bone, which is the textbook case of path-DEPENDENT work: work against friction, viscosity or inelastic deformation depends on the route taken, and dissipation increases with rate. The page's own Consequence line half-catches this - 'The total stress of the re-lattice is not reduced by the spreading, only delayed' - and the register agrees in its Failure line, 'The work is not reduced, only redistributed.' Both say EQUAL. The physics says GREATER, twice over. Thermodynamically, a real transformation dissipates more than the quasistatic minimum and more the faster it runs, so eighteen seconds of spreading lowers the peak and does not return the total. Metabolically, the deferral is anaerobic: glycolysis without oxygen yields 2 ATP per glucose against 30-38 aerobic, and the Cori cycle spends 6 ATP to turn a lactate pair back into one glucose - the pair having earned 2. Borrowing repays at a loss, which is exactly why the cycle cannot be sustained. This also settles the page's own 'What nobody knows', which asks whether the deferred debt is ever smaller than the peak avoided: it is not smaller, and it is larger than the work would have been.

options.option: Correct the Mechanism to cite mechanical advantage without path-independence, and state that the total rises with the rate the transformation was run at.
options.changes: Makes the working's arithmetic honest and answers its open question; means repeated use is strictly worse than the page implies, which is a balance change as well as a wording one.

options.option: Rule with the register that the work is redistributed and exactly conserved, and treat the dissipation surcharge as outside the system's accounting.
options.changes: Keeps Ascensio's Failure line as the governing text and leaves a page whose stated law does not produce its stated behaviour; simplest, and gives up the best answer to the page's open question.

options.option: Answer the 'What nobody knows' line on the page by quoting Ascensio's Failure, and leave the magnitude question open.
options.changes: Smallest edit, closes a question the register already closed, and leaves the equal-or-greater difference between canon and physics recorded rather than decided.

options.option: Make the surcharge mechanical: a stated multiplier on the deferred debt set by how hard and how long the buff was pushed, which the Cost line already gestures at.
options.changes: Turns the physics into a rule and gives the working a scaling cost; needs a number, and neither the system nor the page supplies one.

quote_a: **Effect** · The caster's own skeleton and musculature snap into a higher operating configuration, faster contraction, denser bone, sharper kinetic read, for as long as the buff holds.
quote_b: **Limit** · **One higher configuration at a time.** The body can only be re-latticed into a single state; stacking a second body-morph art on top forces a collision Transmutatio has no clean rule for resolving.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Spinal Forge Ascent.md:19
why: 'Denser bone' at conserved mass is not automatically stronger bone, and whether it is at all depends on a quantity the system never states. Conservation is explicit on the page - 'nothing is created or destroyed' - so densifying at fixed length means thinning: rho times r squared is constant, and doubling density takes the radius to r over root two. Bending strength follows the section modulus Z = pi r cubed over four, which falls to 0.354 of its former value. Against that, bone strength rises with apparent density on a power law, and the measured exponent for human trabecular compressive strength is about 2 (modulus 2 to 3), the standard cellular-solid scaling. Net bending strength is therefore 0.354 times 2^n: a 29 per cent LOSS at n = 1, exactly break-even at n = 1.5, and a 41 per cent gain at the measured n = 2. Bending stiffness is worse - EI with E going as rho^2 to rho^3 against I going as rho^-2 leaves rho^0 to rho^1, so the frame is at best linearly stiffer and possibly not stiffer at all. So the page's central physical claim is true at the measured exponent and false one assumption away, and the system supplies no exponent to settle it. Separately, the page's stated Limit is bookkeeping ('one higher configuration at a time') where the physics offers a hard structural limit it does not use: densification proceeds by compacting the cellular part of bone, trabecular apparent density runs roughly 0.1 to 1.0 g/cm3 against cortical 1.9, and when the spongy volume is spent there is nothing left to compact. That ceiling differs per practitioner, cannot be trained past, and would be a better Limit than the one on the page.

options.option: State a strength-density relation in the Magic System pages, so 'denser' has a determinate sign wherever a working claims it.
options.changes: Settles this page and every future densification working; a new rule, and the honest value (about squared) makes densification a modest gain rather than a dramatic one.

options.option: Add the cortical-density ceiling to the page as a second Limit, stated per practitioner.
options.changes: Gives the working a limit that cannot be worked around and a reason two casters get different results; needs no new system rule, only the page.

options.option: Drop 'denser bone' and keep the muscle half, which carries the working's output on its own.
options.changes: Removes the undetermined claim and costs the page its explanation for why the failure mode is microfractures rather than tearing.

options.option: Rule that a re-lattice changes the material rather than only its packing, so strength is free of the section-modulus trade.
options.changes: Legalises any density claim and quietly abandons 'nothing is created or destroyed', which is the working's own premise and Transmutatio's law.

quote_a: **Target Response** · An observer sees the caster's spine light molten-white, and the caster's subsequent strikes land with force consistent with a full Grade above their unbuffed baseline.
quote_b: **Overchannel Spikes.** The benchmarks above are sustainable output. Overchannel can temporarily spike Strike Force and Lifting Strength by **two to five times** the sustainable ceiling, depending on the Ardency Overchannel Sub-Stat's Grade and the character's tolerance for Crystal Fracture risk. Every Overchannel event deposits structural damage that must be healed through rest, alchemical treatment or Temperance advancement. A character who regularly Overchannels accumulates fracture density that eventually becomes permanent. Some fractures become architectural features. Most become liabilities.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:152
why: The working grants a full Tier Grade and charges a cost that lapses. Part Eleven prices the system's own temporary-output mechanism an order of magnitude lower and charges permanently: Overchannel gives 'two to five times the sustainable ceiling' and 'Every Overchannel event deposits structural damage that must be healed through rest, alchemical treatment or Temperance advancement. A character who regularly Overchannels accumulates fracture density that eventually becomes permanent.' A full Grade is a great deal more than two to five times. Floor to floor, A to S is 4.6024e10 J to 4.184e12 J, a factor of about 91, and the page's own mechanism supports it - a fibre-type shift toward fast glycolytic operation buys 5 to 12 times the shortening velocity, which is 25 to 144 times in impact energy - so the number is not the problem. The price is. This page charges 'microfractures and Essenced muscle fatigue surfacing once the buff lapses', with no accumulation clause and no permanence. The comparison is not incidental: Transmutatio's Stat Effect strengthens 'Ardency Conversion', which the Merge Ledger renames Overchannel, so the working's primary Wellspring strengthens the Sub-Stat whose penalty the page has not applied, and the page never uses the word. Part Four sharpens it further - 'One full Tier Grade above an opponent wins a direct exchange of that stat category without meaningful contest' - so an eighteen-second reliable full-Grade buff is eighteen seconds of guaranteed wins in that category, which is a different proposition from a buff.

options.option: Apply the Overchannel penalty: each use deposits structural damage that must be healed, with accumulation toward permanence, and name Overchannel on the page.
options.changes: Makes the working consistent with the system's own temporary-output rule and expensive to use twice in a week; costs the page its clean 'it lapses' framing, which is what makes it attractive.

options.option: Reduce the gain to Overchannel's 2-5x band and keep the lapsing cost.
options.changes: Consistent and cheap to write; discards the page's best feature, since the full-Grade claim is the only headline number in this volume its own mechanism can pay for.

options.option: Rule that a mass-conserving re-lattice is not Overchannel, because nothing is drawn beyond a sustainable threshold - the body is re-expressed rather than over-driven.
options.changes: Defensible from Transmutatio's law and from the Overchannel definition's own wording, and it opens a route by which any working framed as re-expression escapes the fracture-density clause.

options.option: Keep gain and cost as written and state the constraint as frequency: a stated number of uses before the deferred debt stops clearing.
options.changes: Gives the deferral teeth without importing Overchannel, and is close to what the Cost line already implies with 'scaled to how hard and how long'; needs a number.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Transmutatio's law is change of basis: a coordinate transformation under conservation, where nothing is created or destroyed and a quantity is only re-expressed in a more useful form. Applied to a living skeleton, it re-lattices existing bone and muscle into a denser, higher-output configuration, the same substance differently arranged. Ascensio's law is mechanical advantage, the path-independence of work done against a load: the same total transformation can be made without exceeding what the structure can bear, provided the stress is spread across a longer path instead of taken as one peak. Ascensio spreads the re-lattice's stress across the whole duration of the buff, so the skeleton never takes the full transformation cost in one instant.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · The same object described in two frames yields two entirely different sets of numbers and one unchanged object. Nothing is created or lost in a transformation; the quantities are merely re-expressed. Transmutatio applies this to failed workings, which are not destroyed Essence but Essence in an inconvenient basis, and the Wellspring supplies the transformation that makes them usable again.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Spatium — Spatial Geometry.md:22
why: The page quotes Transmutatio's Analogue accurately and applies the law outside the scope its own register states. The register's Mechanism gives the law and then names what Transmutatio does with it: 'Transmutatio applies this to failed workings, which are not destroyed Essence but Essence in an inconvenient basis, and the Wellspring supplies the transformation that makes them usable again.' Its Stat Effect closes the same loop - 'Failed workings become fuel rather than wounds.' This page applies the law to a living skeleton, which is neither a failed working nor Essence in an inconvenient basis. The change-of-basis mathematics fits what the page wants and the register's stated application does not extend to it, and the page does not say it is extending anything. The consequence that matters is not taxonomic. Transmutatio's Failure is 'Basis loss. The practitioner forgets which frame they started in, and a transformation with no reference frame does not return anything recognisable.' On failed Essence that is a wasted expenditure. On a body it is a practitioner with no frame to revert to, and the page does not acknowledge that the working has a reversion step at all - its stated failures are microfractures, a collapsed schedule and a stacking collision. The most serious unstated risk on the page comes from its own primary Wellspring.

options.option: State the extension on the page: Transmutatio's law applied to living structure rather than to failed workings, with basis loss as a named failure mode.
options.changes: Legitimises the application and gives the working the failure mode it is missing, which is severe and dramatic; makes every use a risk of not changing back.

options.option: Widen the register's Mechanism so Transmutatio applies to any re-expression under conservation, not only to failed workings.
options.changes: Clears this page and any other body-Transmutation art; a change to a Wellspring register, which other pages read as written.

options.option: Re-source the working's primary Wellspring to one whose stated application covers living structure.
options.changes: Keeps both registers intact and costs the page its best-argued paragraph, since change of basis under conservation is exactly the right mathematics for what it describes.

options.option: Leave the scope as it is and treat the register's 'applies this to failed workings' as an example rather than a boundary.
options.changes: No edits, and leaves basis loss unlisted on a body-morph art, which is the outcome a practitioner would most want warned about.

quote_a: **Counterplay** · A Judicium-based kinetic dampener reduces the buff's ceiling directly; timing a heavy strike to land mid-spread forces the whole deferred cost due at once, a worse outcome for the caster than the strike itself.
quote_b: **Analogue** · Emission and absorption spectroscopy. Nondestructive flaw detection.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fulguria — Electromagnetism.md:21
why: The page's Counterplay line names 'A Judicium-based kinetic dampener', and its Weakness line names 'A soul-based kinetic suppression'. Judicium is The Wellspring of Truth in Fulguria, whose Analogue is 'Emission and absorption spectroscopy. Nondestructive flaw detection' and whose Mechanism identifies composition from signature alone. It is an instrument of identification: it reads without acting, which is the whole point of nondestructive inspection. Nothing in its register damps anything, and kinetic damping belongs to Vectoria, the Family of Mechanics, which is this working's own secondary Family. The Origin line repeats the error as established fact - the source's 'Counters & Interactions list (Judicium dampeners, Verdantia stabilization, Titan-forge martial synergy)' - so a countermeasure the page treats as documented is attributed to a Wellspring that cannot perform it. 'Soul-based kinetic suppression' has no register behind it either; suppression in the sixty-four is Harmonics Suppression, which is self-masking, and the Counterplay register's suppression routes are Silence and the anchor routes. This matters because the dampener is one of only two stated counters and is described as reducing the buff's ceiling directly, which is the strongest counterplay claim on the page.

options.option: Re-attribute the dampener to Vectoria, whose Physics Domain is Mechanics and which this page already cross-lists as its secondary Family.
options.changes: Smallest correction, makes the counter performable, and neatly turns the working's own secondary Family into its counter, which is good design.

options.option: Keep Judicium and change what it does on this page: it reads the schedule rather than damping it, and the reduction comes from being read.
options.changes: Stays inside Judicium's actual law - nondestructive detection of a flaw under the paint is a good description of finding a deferral schedule - and weakens the counter from a direct ceiling reduction to an information advantage.

options.option: Replace both counters with routes the Counterplay register already names, and drop 'soul-based kinetic suppression'.
options.changes: Puts the page on attested machinery and loses the flavour of a specialist countermeasure culture, which the Origin line uses as evidence the art is documented.

options.option: Leave both terms as in-world trade names that do not describe the Wellspring accurately.
options.changes: No edits, and leaves a stated counter that a reader checking the register will find cannot work, on a page whose counters are otherwise its strongest feature.

quote_a: No deviser, era, or founding problem is given in the source, beyond the note above on the unrelated card fragment appended after it in the raw export. The source's own Counters & Interactions list (Judicium dampeners, Verdantia stabilization, Titan-forge martial synergy) reads as already-established countermeasures rather than something an opponent worked out live against one caster; per the named-inventor rule that is the signature of a documented technique, not a self-derived one. It is filed as a documented body-Transmutation art of unrecorded, anonymous authorship, taught and studied rather than invented fresh in the scene where it first appears. No deviser's name is invented to fill the gap the card leaves.
quote_b: **Numerical Effect** · Stage VII carries a Stat Ceiling of 475 on the FOW scale; the buff's own floor sits at A-Grade, Stat Range 276 to 400. Duration once ignited: three exchanges, roughly eighteen seconds.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Spinal Forge Ascent.md:39
why: The Origin line refers to something the page does not contain: 'beyond the note above on the unrelated card fragment appended after it in the raw export'. There is no such note above. The mirrored page runs Summary card, Codex line, Design Chain, FOW line, Origin and nothing else, so either the reference is stale or the wiki mirror has dropped a block that the Notion source carries - and the block in question is described as an unrelated card fragment, which is exactly the kind of content a converter would strip. This is recorded rather than argued because it bears on whether this account has read the whole page: an appended fragment could carry a practitioner, a date or a second working, any of which would change the account. The page is otherwise internally complete and nothing in the five sections depends on the missing note.

options.option: Check the Notion source for the appended fragment and either restore it to the mirror or remove the reference.
options.changes: Settles it definitively; a mirror or a source edit rather than a canon decision.

options.option: Remove the dangling clause from the Origin line and leave the rest as written.
options.changes: Smallest edit and loses the record that something was once appended here, which may matter if the fragment turns up elsewhere.

options.option: Leave it and treat the clause as a converter artefact.
options.changes: No edits; every future account of this page inherits the same uncertainty about whether it has the whole text.

quote_a: **Target Response** · The chosen action either misfires, bends back along its own Wellspring vector onto its caster, or splinters into harmless light and sound.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four, attack-output band for A-Grade
why: Refraction conserves energy and scattering conserves energy; neither destroys a joule. The page's own Grade line requires A-Grade, and Part Four puts A-Grade attack output at 4.6024x10^10 to 4.184x10^12 J. Take the floor. Disposed as light and sound from a point over one second, 46 GJ gives a fluence at ten metres of 4.6e10 / (4*pi*10^2) = 3.7x10^7 J/m^2. That is about 27,000 times the solar constant (1,361 W/m^2), roughly 150 times the ~2.5x10^5 J/m^2 threshold for second-degree thermal burns, and as sound it is 10*log10(3.7e7/1e-12) = 196 dB, a peak pressure of sqrt(3.7e7 * 413) = 1.2x10^5 Pa, or 1.2 atmospheres of overpressure, against a lung-injury threshold near 70 kPa. In ordnance terms 46 GJ is 11 tonnes of TNT and the A-Grade ceiling of 4.184 TJ is one kiloton. The word 'harmless' is therefore off by roughly five orders of magnitude, and the Master Glyph Index states the general principle the page is breaking: 'The glyph ends. The law does not. Everything a working produces goes on obeying every rule it has ever obeyed.' The other two stated outcomes balance fine - a deviated attack lands somewhere, a reflected one lands on its caster - so this is one word in one clause and not a failure of the working's design.

options.option: Rewrite the third outcome as dispersal rather than annihilation: the attack becomes incoherent and is released over a stated volume and time, with the blast and thermal figures stated.
options.changes: Keeps the mechanism exactly (it is Aurevane's phase-locking clause read backwards) and makes the third outcome the most dangerous one on the page rather than the safest, which changes how a practitioner would choose to use it and gives opponents a reason to prefer being deviated.

options.option: Remove the third outcome and leave two, deviation and retroreflection, both of which conserve honestly.
options.changes: Costs the page its most evocative line and removes the outcome the card's own Effect wording ('fail catastrophically') leans on; simplifies the working to a single interface with two regimes.

options.option: Rule that the working returns the attack's energy to the target's own reserve rather than radiating it, so the disposal is an Essence transaction and not a thermal one.
options.changes: Closes the physics and introduces a new mechanic the system does not currently state - energy returning to a Crystal as EU - which would need a rule of its own and would affect every redirection working in the corpus.

options.option: Cap the working's Grade by the energy it can safely disperse rather than by the practitioner's Stage, and state the cap.
options.changes: Makes the working scale-limited instead of Stage-limited, which is a new kind of gate for the system, and would mean an A-Grade practitioner cannot use it against an A-Grade attack.

quote_a: **Cost** · Resonance Strain after three uses in a scene, and Perception Debt that splits her hearing between echoes of past and future chords afterward.
quote_b: > **Costs the card states, kept whole.** *High-output use of Symphonia Ascendant causes minor temporal fractures in her internal reality field, requiring intensive Oneirion meditation to realign.* **Activating the Temporal Chord spends a significant and irreversible portion of Crystalline Recall's stored memories, leaving permanent memory gaps upon repeated use.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:90
why: Two documents price the same named working differently. The technique page charges 'Resonance Strain after three uses in a scene, and Perception Debt that splits her hearing between echoes of past and future chords afterward' - a temporary precision penalty, in two terms the corpus does not define anywhere else. Her card, naming Symphonia Ascendant explicitly, charges something structural and slow: 'High-output use of Symphonia Ascendant causes minor temporal fractures in her internal reality field, requiring intensive Oneirion meditation to realign.' The card's cost is the one that hurts, and it hurts the thing she is defined by - a High Archivist of Resonance whose archive is degrading - while the page's cost is an inconvenience that clears by the next scene. This is not a difference of emphasis: one document says the working costs her recovery time and the other says it costs her record. The card is the later-edited document (2026-09-23 against the page's 2026-09-12), which under the reading rule would ordinarily settle it, but the page's terms are not a subset of the card's and nothing in either text says one supersedes the other.

options.option: Adopt the card's cost on the technique page and drop the page's two terms.
options.changes: Gives the working a cost that hurts and passes the fairness check; removes the 'three uses in a scene' counter, which is the only usage cap the page states, so a limit would have to be restated some other way.

options.option: Keep both as two different costs at two different scales - the page's tremor per scene, the card's temporal fracture on high-output use - and define which uses count as high-output.
options.changes: Preserves both documents and adds a threshold the system must then state; the page's four undefined terms still need attestation (SA-UNATT-SYMPHONIA-VOCABULARY).

options.option: Rule that the card governs costs for any working the card names by name, and technique pages govern only workings the card does not price.
options.changes: Settles this row and a class of others across the corpus with one general rule; makes a number of technique pages' Cost lines advisory, which is a large change to how the pages are read.

options.option: Keep the page's cost and strike the clause from the card.
options.changes: Cheapest edit and the wrong direction on fairness: it removes the only stated consequence that persists past a scene for her signature working, and the card's clause is written as characterisation rather than bookkeeping.

quote_a: **Effect** · Binds a polyphonic chord of sigils to a target's Essence pattern and, on their next offensive action, forces a misfire, a self-directed backlash, or a total refraction into harmless light or sound.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · This runs on real resonant coupling and vector decomposition. A system tuned to a matching frequency can be driven by it, and a force's direction is a variable that can be reassigned without destroying the force itself. The sigils act as the coupling medium; the redirection is the vector's own components sent somewhere other than their intended target.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Symphonia Ascendant.md:31
why: The Effect line promises three outcomes: a misfire, a self-directed backlash, and a total refraction into harmless light or sound. The Mechanism line supplies one operation: 'a force's direction is a variable that can be reassigned without destroying the force itself... the redirection is the vector's own components sent somewhere other than their intended target.' A vector reassignment produces the backlash cleanly - reverse the vector - and produces a deviation cleanly. It does not produce a misfire, which is a failure to fire and therefore an amplitude or phase fault rather than a direction fault, and it does not produce a splintering into light and sound, which is the loss of the phase relationship across a wavefront and again not a direction fault. So two of the three stated outcomes are not operations the stated mechanism performs. The card, interestingly, states a mechanism that does cover all three: 'The waves impose a refractive law on the target's internal Aether.' One refractive interface produces deviation below the critical angle, total internal reflection above it, and incoherent scatter at a rough or graded boundary - three regimes of one law, selected by angle of incidence. The page has the right effect list and the narrower mechanism; the card has the wider mechanism and no effect list.

options.option: Replace the page's Mechanism with the card's refractive-interface reading, and state that the three outcomes are three regimes of one interface selected by angle of incidence.
options.changes: Makes the effect list follow from the mechanism with nothing left over, brings the page into line with the card, and gives the working a stated variable (angle of incidence) that an opponent could in principle influence - which is new counterplay the page does not currently have.

options.option: Narrow the Effect line to what vector reassignment produces: deviation and self-directed backlash only.
options.changes: Smallest edit; costs the page its third outcome, which is also the outcome SA-PHYS-SYMPHONIA-HARMLESS-LIGHT says does not balance, so the two rows could be closed by the same decision.

options.option: Keep both and add a second stated operation - a phase or coherence attack alongside the vector one - naming which Wellspring supplies each.
options.changes: Honest to the registers, since Aurevane is the phase-locking current and Mirithane the reflection one; makes the working explicitly two mechanisms and raises the question of whether it should cost more.

options.option: Rule that 'misfire' here means a deviation severe enough to miss entirely rather than a failure to fire.
options.changes: Resolves two thirds of the row by definition at no cost to either document, and leaves the light-and-sound outcome still unexplained by the stated mechanism.

quote_a: **Counterplay** · Field an Anchor Ward before her chord locks on, or force the exchange through a Fate-locked Edict, which the working can only soften rather than redirect.
quote_b: Every system term comes from the Lexicon of Magic / Core Vocabulary.
path_b: imports/system-accounts/_method.md, and wiki/The Magic System/The Lexicon of Magic — Master Terminology.md
why: Four terms on this page occur nowhere else in the corpus: 'Anchor Ward', 'Perception Debt', 'Resonance Strain' and 'Fate-locked Edict'. A full-text search across wiki/ returns this page and no other file for each of the four. That would be a minor filing matter except for where they sit. 'Resonance Strain' and 'Perception Debt' are the page's entire Cost line (:37). 'Anchor Ward' and 'Fate-locked Edict' are the page's entire Counter line (:38) and half its Summary-card Counter (:20). So the working's price and the working's counters - the two things a player would have to look up to beat it, and the two things the fairness check turns on - are written in vocabulary that has no entry anywhere. A player following the lookup trail for 'Anchor Ward' finds this page telling them to field one and nothing at all telling them what one is. Note what is not in this row: 'Fate Path' and 'Edict' are both attested, so 'Fate-locked Edict' may be a compound of attested parts rather than a new term; the other three have no attested parts at all.

options.option: Write register entries for the four terms, in the Lexicon or the Counterplay page as appropriate.
options.changes: Closes the row and adds four pieces of lookupable system, one of which - a ward that detunes rather than blocks - is a counter-form the corpus does not currently carry and several other workings could use.

options.option: Restate the page's Cost and Counter lines in attested vocabulary only.
options.changes: Cheapest, and the attested replacements exist: the detuning ward is Counterplay's 'Lock' ('occupies a limit so no other limit can be set there'), the chaotic-pattern counter is 'Knot', and the cost can be taken from the card. Costs the page four coinages that read well.

options.option: Rule that a technique page may coin a term for a counter or a cost provided it is defined in the same page.
options.changes: Legitimises a practice several pages in this batch already follow and creates a standing obligation to define in place; does not fix this page, which defines none of the four.

options.option: Rule the four attested by use, since they appear in a published page.
options.changes: Removes this class of conflict across the corpus at a stroke and removes the lookup trail with it, since a term attested only by the page that uses it cannot be looked up anywhere else.

quote_a: Governing Primary Dominion (Sense, Radius) and Harmonics (Attunement). Stage floor VII, Refraction. Grade required A-Grade (late push toward S-Grade). Path gate Spirit Path. Resonant Pair none indicated in the source.
quote_b: **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Gnosis Perception, Vigilance, Harmonics Fidelity. What you see becomes truer. What you express becomes more accurate.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fulguria — Electromagnetism.md:30 (Aurevane), with Mirithane at wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:44
why: The page declares two Wellsprings, Aurevane primary and Mirithane secondary, and then governs on three Sub-Stats: Dominion Sense, Dominion Radius and Harmonics Attunement. Aurevane strengthens Gnosis Perception, Gnosis Vigilance and Harmonics Fidelity; Mirithane strengthens Harmonics Fidelity and Tempering Coherence. Under the Merge Ledger, Fidelity reads as Attunement and Coherence as Anchoring. So the two declared registers yield Gnosis Perception, Gnosis Vigilance, Harmonics Attunement and Resilience Anchoring. Attunement is accounted for. Dominion Sense and Dominion Radius are not, and both belong to other currents on the same character card: Dominion Sense to Abyntheus ('Dominion Sovereignty, Dominion Sense, Gnosis Cognition') and Dominion Reach, which reads as Sovereignty, to Oneirion ('Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Reach, Ardency Spectral'). This matters because Dominion Radius is what carries the working's five kilometres. The page's reach is supplied by a Sub-Stat whose current the page does not declare, which means either the Wellspring line is incomplete or the FOW line is reaching past it.

options.option: Add Abyntheus and Oneirion to the page's Wellspring line as the currents carrying the Dominion half.
options.changes: Makes the FOW line derivable and matches the card, which carries both; raises the working's harmonisation load from two currents to four and brings Oneirion's and Abyntheus's failure modes onto the page with them.

options.option: Drop Dominion Sense and Dominion Radius from the FOW line and govern on Harmonics and Gnosis only.
options.changes: Keeps the two declared Wellsprings honest; costs the page its stated five-kilometre reach, which would then have to be re-derived from something else or dropped.

options.option: Rule that a working's governing Sub-Stats need not be strengthened by its declared Wellsprings, being a property of the practitioner rather than of the current.
options.changes: Would close a recurring class of rows across this batch in one move, and would sever the link the Wellspring registers currently carry between a current and what it strengthens, which is how most technique pages derive their FOW lines.

options.option: Re-derive the reach from Harmonics Projection, whose gate ('Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C for field weight and Stage VI to exceed A for reach') at least names reach, and state it.
options.changes: Keeps the reach with a Sub-Stat the page could plausibly claim from Mirithane's line; runs straight into the Attraction Path question already logged as SA-CROSS-SPECULUM-ATTRACTION-PATH.

quote_a: **Limit** · She has to have heard or felt the target cast before the sigils have anything to link to, and it does not touch a purely mundane attack.
quote_b: **Crystalline Recall** · **Records and replays a working's complete emotional signature and Essence flow as a living memory.** *Used to mimic, teach, or deceive.* **The [Ma] Recall glyphs in her eyes are this trait made visible.**
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:88
why: The page's headline limit is that she must have heard or felt the target cast before the sigils have anything to link to. As physics that is correct and unavoidable - a driven resonance only couples inside a bandwidth you have measured (the account's section 1a). As a limit on the character it is close to empty, because of her own Trait. Crystalline Recall 'records and replays a working's complete emotional signature and Essence flow as a living memory' and is 'used to mimic, teach, or deceive'. So the prior read is: recorded rather than remembered; permanent rather than decaying; obtainable at the working's own five kilometres without her being present at the fight, since the page's own channel is Aetheric and not acoustic (an acoustic read at 5 km arrives at about -14 dB against a 30-40 dB floor and 14.6 seconds late); and transferable, because 'teach' is in the Trait's own text. A limit that is satisfied once, forever, from an archive, and can be handed to somebody else is not a limit an opponent can act on. The page's other limit - 'it does not touch a purely mundane attack' - is genuine and unworkaroundable, which is why this row is about one clause and not about the working.

options.option: State that a Crystalline Recall record decays, or is consumed on use, for the purpose of satisfying this working's prior-read condition.
options.changes: Restores the limit and gives an opponent a reason to force her to spend records; conflicts with the Trait's own wording, which is about permanence, and the card already spends Recall records to pay for the Temporal Chord, so the two drains would need reconciling.

options.option: Require the prior read to be of the specific working being redirected, not of the practitioner, so each new technique in an opponent's repertoire has to be heard separately.
options.changes: Keeps the archive and makes the limit bite in the only place it matters - an opponent who varies his repertoire beats her - and matches the physics, since two workings of one practitioner need not share a resonant line.

options.option: Require presence: the read must be taken within some stated distance, at the time of casting, rather than from a record.
options.changes: Makes the limit costly and forces her into engagements before she can act in them; contradicts nothing in the Trait but does contradict the page's 'heard or felt', which is what currently lets the read be Aetheric.

options.option: Leave the limit as written and accept that it constrains only the first exchange against a given opponent.
options.changes: No edit, and it should then be said plainly on the page, because as written the limit reads to a player as a per-fight condition and is in fact a once-per-lifetime one.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Eight-metre displacement, instant. The strike that follows draws on his documented Ardency 320 (A-Grade): peak force in the 20–100 GN range, 46 GJ to 4 TJ yield, city-block-scale output at full commitment, though an ambush strike is a fraction of that ceiling rather than the full spike.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · Tenebra's real operation is signal-to-noise reduction: an absorptive coating across the Aether Shell plus a faceted return geometry that sends what little signal does reflect away from the observer, so Draven is not invisible, only quieter than the background. Petralon's kinetic ignition supplies the launch; his Shell converts stored Essence into a single directed impulse that carries him the eight metres while the Tenebra coating keeps the transit itself below the quarry's noise floor. He is not there, and then, having spent the impulse, he is here, already loaded into the strike.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Tenebra Ambush Art.md:38
why: The working's premise is that the transit stays below the quarry's noise floor. Its stated speed makes the transit the loudest event in the scene. Eight metres 'in an instant' - read as 0.1 s, which is what instant means in an exchange - is a mean speed of 80 m/s for a body of roughly 100 kg (the corpus gives no mass; 100 kg is an assumption for a 1.95 m man described as lean, dense, heavily scarred muscle). Drag at that speed is 0.5*1.225*80^2*1.0*0.7 = 2.7 kN, dissipating 220 kW of drag power. A solid body moving subsonically radiates as a Curle dipole with acoustic efficiency scaling as M^3; at M = 80/343 = 0.233 that is 1.27x10^-2, so radiated acoustic power is of order 10^1 to 10^3 W, which over a sphere of radius 8 m is roughly 105 to 125 dB. The Tenebra coating has no authority over any of it: the register's mechanism conditions what returns off the Shell ('absorbing incident energy and by shaping surfaces so the little that reflects goes anywhere except back at the observer'), and this noise is emitted, not reflected. The same arithmetic prices the fix, because drag power goes as v^3 and dipole efficiency as M^3, so radiated acoustic power goes as the sixth power of transit speed: crossing the same eight metres in 0.8 s instead of 0.1 s is 8^6 = 262,000 times quieter, 54 dB down, into the fifties. The mechanical side moves with it - 1.07 MN of ground reaction and 17.8 MPa under the boots at 0.1 s against 16.7 kN and 0.28 MPa at 0.8 s, where ordinary soil bears about 0.2 MPa. The system has already noticed: Part Seven's Dexterity gate prices 'suppression of kinetic noise and Aura spill' at Attraction Path, Stage V, to exceed S, and Draven's Feint peak is 386, A-Grade, one Grade below the clause.

options.option: State a transit time long enough for the noise to sit under a realistic floor - of order 0.5-1 s for the eight metres - and keep 'instant' as what it feels like to the quarry rather than what it is.
options.changes: Closes the physics with one number and keeps every other claim on the page; costs the working its most striking line and makes it a fast approach rather than a displacement, which is a different tactical object.

options.option: Give the working a second Tenebra-side clause that suppresses emitted noise as well as reflected signal, and pay for it.
options.changes: Keeps the speed; requires the Sub-Stat Part Seven already names for exactly this ('suppression of kinetic noise and Aura spill', S-Grade, Attraction Path), which Draven does not have at either the Grade or the Path, so it would also require a change to his sheet.

options.option: Keep the speed and the noise, and rewrite the working as an ambush that trades silence for the quarry having no time to use what it hears.
options.changes: Honest and playable - 0.1 s is inside human reaction time, so a loud crossing can still work - but it inverts the page's own Function line and makes the Tenebra half decorative during the transit rather than load-bearing.

options.option: Rule that Aether Shell suppression covers emitted mechanical noise as well as reflected signal, generally.
options.changes: Resolves this row and a class of others across the corpus at once; makes every stealth working in the register much stronger and removes acoustic detection as a counterplay route, which the Counterplay page currently relies on for several cases.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Tenebra's real operation is signal-to-noise reduction: an absorptive coating across the Aether Shell plus a faceted return geometry that sends what little signal does reflect away from the observer, so Draven is not invisible, only quieter than the background. Petralon's kinetic ignition supplies the launch; his Shell converts stored Essence into a single directed impulse that carries him the eight metres while the Tenebra coating keeps the transit itself below the quarry's noise floor. He is not there, and then, having spent the impulse, he is here, already loaded into the strike.
quote_b: **Analogue** · Compressive load path and creep. Stone in compression; the arch. **Mechanism** · Masonry is enormously strong in compression and nearly worthless in tension, which is why the arch exists: it converts a span into a queue of compressive members. Petralon reorganises the Crystal along the same principle, routing every incoming load into compression and accepting slow creep deformation as the price of never developing a tensile crack. **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Vitality Endurance, Dominion Gravity. The character becomes the ground beneath the ground.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md, Petralon
why: The technique page says 'Petralon's kinetic ignition supplies the launch', and Draven's card agrees, listing 'Petralon - Vectoria. The kinetic ignition.' The register says Petralon is the arch: a compressive load path, strengthening Vitality Endurance and Dominion Gravity, glossed as 'the character becomes the ground beneath the ground'. That is not a launch current; it is the current that does not move. Nothing in the register mentions propulsion, impulse, or acceleration. The correction is available and improves the page rather than costing it. An eight-metre crossing at the page's stated speed puts of order 1.07 MN of ground reaction through two legs (see SA-PHYS-TENEBRA-TRANSIT-NOISE), against a femur that fails in compression near 10 kN, so something must route that load as compression without developing a tensile crack - which is Petralon's register clause word for word. And the ignition itself is on the card under a different heading and is not a Wellspring at all: the Trait 'Vorynn Bloodbind - Through an ancestral pact, his blood can ignite his muscles with primal, predatory force', with the Aether Shell as conduit ('Channels Aether into hyper-dense muscular ignition and aggressive kinetic force'). Reading it that way also imports Petralon's Failure, 'Tensile exposure ... It parts', which lands on the arrest at the far end rather than the launch, and gives the working a failure mode it currently lacks.

options.option: Restate Petralon's role on the page and the card as load-bearing rather than propulsive, and credit the ignition to the Vorynn Bloodbind and the Shell.
options.changes: Brings both documents into line with the register, gives the working a stated failure mode (tensile exposure on arrest), and - because the Bloodbind's price is Primal Regression - supplies the cost this page currently lacks, closing SA-FAIR-TENEBRA-NO-COST with the same edit.

options.option: Amend Petralon's register entry to include a propulsive clause.
options.changes: Keeps four documents unchanged and changes one, but the entry's whole construction is the arch, and a current that both launches and grounds is no longer the analogue it is written from; it would also alter every other page that draws on Petralon.

options.option: Replace Petralon on this page with a Vectoria current whose register does supply impulse, and keep Petralon as a third harmonisation for the load path.
options.changes: Most faithful to the registers; raises his harmonisation count, which his own card already flags as above his Tempering Capacity at this Stage, and requires naming a current the page does not currently carry.

options.option: Rule that a card's Wellspring gloss governs over the register where the two disagree about what a current does.
options.changes: Settles this row and a class of others in one move; inverts the usual direction, since the registers are the general law and the cards are the instances, and would make each card's one-line glosses load-bearing rules.

quote_a: **Grade required** · A-Grade
quote_b: **Law V, the Law of Material Anchor, is a Stage gate rather than a universal.** Below **Stage VII, Refraction**, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md:201
why: The page declares Craft Spellcraft and Stage floor VI, Glory. Stage VI is below Refraction, so Law V binds and the working requires an external anchor: voice, hand, ink or blood. The page names none. This is not pedantry on an ambush page, because the Four Crafts distinguishes two anchors that are opposite in exactly the property this technique is built on. Spellcraft's instrument in the crafts table is 'a mouth'. Its Bodily delivery vector is the other option: 'A fist with combustion on it is Spellcraft with the body as the pen, and the sentence is still ephemeral - which is why the fist stops burning the moment attention lapses.' An ambush working anchored on a spoken chain announces itself before it runs and hands an opponent Counterplay's 'Interrupt the chain' with a hand over the mouth; an ambush working anchored on the body does neither. The page's sister technique on the same practitioner states its vector explicitly ('Spellcraft (Bodily: the fist carries the working, and it stops the instant his attention lapses)', Vorynn Execution Strike), which shows the corpus knows the distinction and that this page has simply not made it. Note the page is otherwise the best of Draven's four on Craft: it names a real craft where three of his pages name the umbrella (SA-CROSS-DRAVEN-CRAFT-SPLIT).

options.option: State the Bodily delivery vector on the page, as Vorynn Execution Strike does.
options.changes: One clause; removes the spoken-anchor interrupt and makes the working consistent with its own stealth premise. Also imports the Bodily clause's own limit - the sentence stops when attention lapses - which is a real constraint mid-transit.

options.option: State a spoken or gestural anchor and accept the tell.
options.changes: Gives the working the counterplay it is thinnest on and makes the dark it launches from a place an opponent can listen to; costs it some of its silence, which is the thing it is for.

options.option: Raise the working's Stage floor to VII so Law V does not bind.
options.changes: Removes the question and takes the technique away from its own practitioner, who is Stage VI at the floor; also contradicts the page's stated floor and Grade.

options.option: Rule that a working whose whole function is suppression is exempt from the audible forms of the Law V anchor.
options.changes: Closes this and every other stealth page below Refraction; creates a category of workings that escape the most-used route in the Counterplay register, which is a large change to how Stage VII is taught to matter.

quote_a: **Cost** · Essence drawn through the Tenebra/Petralon combination surfaces as a mild drip from eyes and nose. Overuse is not costed further on his sheet; per standing drawback rules, "it strains him" alone is not treated as a real cost, and none beyond the documented drip is claimed here.
quote_b: > **Risk · Primal Regression.** *Over-reliance on the Vorynn Bloodbind risks triggering an uncontrolled metamorphosis into a Prime Beast form, resulting in permanent loss of sapience and systemic collapse.*
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Draven Kael Vorrick · The Beast Slayer.md:37
why: The page prices an eight-metre repositioning that arrives unseen and already mid-strike, usable at will, at a nosebleed - and then says itself that this is not a cost: 'per standing drawback rules, "it strains him" alone is not treated as a real cost, and none beyond the documented drip is claimed here.' The page's honesty is exactly right and the gap is still a gap: on the fairness test 'costs something that hurts' this working fails, and it fails on the one of Draven's techniques that is most usable, most repeatable, and least answerable once it has started. The cost is available one heading away on his own card, and the route to it is the same correction SA-CROSS-TENEBRA-PETRALON-ROLE proposes. If the launch is not Petralon but the Vorynn Bloodbind - the card's only Trait, 'his blood can ignite his muscles with primal, predatory force' - then the working is a Bloodbind use and carries the Bloodbind's stated price: 'Risk - Primal Regression. Over-reliance on the Vorynn Bloodbind risks triggering an uncontrolled metamorphosis into a Prime Beast form, resulting in permanent loss of sapience and systemic collapse.' The card's own commentary calls that 'the cleanest stated cost on any Volume IV sheet. It is not a resource drain. It is an ending, and he knows the shape of it.' A technique that draws on it is costed; a technique that does not is not.

options.option: Credit the launch to the Vorynn Bloodbind and state that every use advances Primal Regression.
options.changes: Closes the fairness gap with an existing canon cost rather than a new one, and makes the ambush a resource he has to ration; also closes SA-CROSS-TENEBRA-PETRALON-ROLE with the same edit.

options.option: Add a stated per-scene or per-use cap - a number of crossings before the ignition stops answering.
options.changes: Gives an opponent something to count and a reason to make him spend; introduces a usage-cap mechanic the system does not currently state in general terms.

options.option: Price the cost in the mechanical damage the crossing actually does to him at the stated speed - roughly 1,090 g of launch acceleration through the frame - and state it as accumulating structural harm.
options.changes: Ties the cost to the number that is already wrong (SA-PHYS-TENEBRA-TRANSIT-NOISE), so slowing the crossing would cheapen it, which is a satisfying coupling and a second dial to balance.

options.option: Accept the drip as the cost on the grounds that the working's real limit is the field condition rather than the reserve.
options.changes: No edit; leaves the working free to use whenever a dim zone exists, which on the pages Draven appears in is most of the time, and leaves the fairness test failed on the record.

page: (3 pages: Tenebra Ambush Art, Vorynn Execution Strike, Winter Rend)
quote_a: **Feint** requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B, with suppression of kinetic noise and Aura spill requiring Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed S.
path_a: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Seven, Dexterity Gates
quote_b: What is not visible from outside is that an Axis is a load-bearing member. The architecture built on it has to stand up whether or not the person is still alive to stand under it. Every Prime Instructor has seen what a Flourished practitioner does the year their Axis dies, and the answer is not that the power fails. The power is fine. The power is entirely fine and it is still shaped exactly like a bond to somebody who is not there.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Sixteen Stages.md:96
why: Draven's declared Path is Body, on his card and on all three of his pages in this batch. His highest Dexterity Sub-Stat is Silence 386, which reads as Feint under the Merge Ledger and is A-Grade, and Part Seven gates Feint above B on Spirit Path. So on the face of it his signature stealth Sub-Stat is gated on a Path he does not hold. His card does not leave this alone; it raises it and gives an answer of a different kind: 'Harmonics 124 in a Stage VI practitioner, and Stage IV requires a Spirit Axis to reach. Draven had one. He does not now.' The Sixteen Stages backs that up - Stage IV's Catalyst is 'formation of the first genuine Spirit Axis, a bond with another soul that carries mechanical weight in the Harmonics' - and states that the architecture survives its loss: 'the power does not fail when the Axis dies.' What the system does not say anywhere is whether an Axis, live or dead, satisfies a Path gate. The Four Paths is emphatic that 'Path commitment is not declared. It is recognised', which suggests behaviour rather than history, and a man who built a Stage IV on a Spirit Axis had Spirit-routed behaviour at the time. Nothing says whether he still does, or whether the structure built then continues to authorise. The question is not local to one page: it decides whether three of Draven's techniques pass their gates, and the same shape will recur for every Flourished practitioner in the corpus whose Axis is gone.

options.option: Rule that an Axis, live or dead, satisfies Path gates for any architecture built while it stood, and nothing built after.
options.changes: Passes Draven's existing Sub-Stats and freezes his future ones; gives 'the power does not fail when the Axis dies' a precise mechanical meaning and makes the year an Axis dies a hard ceiling on a practitioner's development, which is a strong and playable rule.

options.option: Rule that an Axis is not a Path and gates are checked against current commitment only.
options.changes: Clean, and it fails Draven's Feint at 386 across three pages, which would mean either a Path change on his card or a Sub-Stat reduction; also means every Flourished practitioner loses gate access the year their Axis dies, which contradicts 'the power is entirely fine'.

options.option: Rule that a dead Axis satisfies gates at a reduced effective Grade - one band down - so the architecture stands but degrades.
options.changes: Splits the difference and matches the Sixteen Stages' tone about what such a practitioner becomes; introduces a new degradation mechanic that would have to be priced and tracked.

options.option: Leave the two systems independent and say so explicitly in Part Seven.
options.changes: Costs nothing and closes the gap as a gap rather than as a rule, leaving every affected sheet to be settled case by case, which is where this batch keeps arriving.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · The real phenomenon underneath is selective permeability, the same principle a semipermeable membrane or a tuned filter uses: the barrier does not resist everything equally, it resists whatever fails a specific test, and passes whatever matches the standard set at construction. Judicium supplies the verdict-law that runs the test on every incoming force; Sublimatio supplies the refining step that separates what passes cleanly from what is arrested, purified or annihilated, in the same way a sublimation vessel separates a purified vapor from the residue that never rises. The barrier is a standing Density working, held open rather than fired.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four, travel-speed column
why: The page's mechanism is selective permeability, correctly named: the barrier 'does not resist everything equally, it resists whatever fails a specific test'. A test implies a response, and a response in a crystalline shell cannot propagate faster than the speed of sound in that shell. Representative longitudinal wave speeds: steel 5,900 m/s, quartz 5,700, alumina about 10,000, diamond about 18,000. Take the best crystalline case, 10,000 m/s: across the stated 7 m radius, the ward needs 0.7 ms to signal across itself. Part Four puts A-Grade travel speed - the working's own required Grade - at Mach 5 to 25, which is 1,715 to 8,575 m/s. At the top of its own band an incoming attack is moving at 86 percent of the ward's internal signal speed and crosses the full radius in the time the ward would need to tell one part of itself about another. One Grade up it stops being close: S-Grade travel is Mach 25 to 200, 8,575 to 68,600 m/s, up to seven times the ward's signal speed. A barrier whose selectivity depends on responding differently to different arrivals cannot be selective about something supersonic in its own lattice; against anything at or above that speed it is a plain wall, and a plain wall is what the page's own 'enough raw kinetic weight can fracture it outright' describes. This is not a flaw so much as an unstated ceiling, and it happens to explain why the working sits at A-Grade.

options.option: State the speed ceiling on the page: the ward tests what arrives below the speed of sound in its own lattice and merely resists what arrives above it.
options.changes: Gives the working a hard, findable, quantitative limit and a second counterplay route that any fast attacker already owns; makes the barrier explicitly two-mode, which the page currently writes as one.

options.option: Raise the ward's material so its signal speed clears its own Grade band - a diamond-class lattice at ~18,000 m/s clears A-Grade with margin and still fails against S.
options.changes: Keeps one mode and pushes the ceiling up one Grade; requires the page to state what the shell is made of, which it currently does not, and the ceiling still exists one step higher.

options.option: Rule that a Judicium verdict is not a mechanical response and propagates at the working's own Aetheric rate rather than at sound speed in the substrate.
options.changes: Removes the ceiling entirely and requires the system to state a propagation speed for a verdict, which it currently does nowhere; that number would then govern every reactive ward in the corpus.

options.option: Keep the ward selective only within a shell much thinner than its radius, so nothing needs to cross it.
options.changes: Physically the cleanest fix - a local test needs no global signal - and it costs the page its 'static field 3 to 7 m' framing, since the selective element becomes a surface rather than a volume.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · A static field 3 to 7 m around the caster, holding for an estimated three sustained exchanges of incoming pressure, on the order of ten to fifteen seconds continuous, an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives duration only in the old system's "turns." At the required A-Grade the barrier's arrest capacity sits at the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark, tens of giganewtons of peak force before failure.
quote_b: **Durability**, capacity to absorb, deflect or endure incoming energy without structural failure
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md, the five facets of Physical Force
why: The page states the ward's capacity as a force: 'tens of giganewtons of peak force before failure', correctly read off Part Eleven's A-Grade Strike Force row of 20-100 GN. A shell does not fail at a force; it fails where the stress exceeds the material's strength, and stress is force per unit area. Run the arithmetic over the page's own radii. The shell area is 4*pi*r^2: 113 m^2 at r = 3 m, 616 m^2 at r = 7 m. Spread over the whole surface, 20 GN is 177 MPa at the small radius and 32 MPa at the large one; 100 GN is 884 MPa and 162 MPa. Those are entirely reasonable numbers for a crystalline shell - structural steel yields at 250-550 MPa and alumina takes 2-3 GPa in compression - so the page's capacity is a genuine pass when the load is distributed. Concentrate the same force on a square centimetre and it is 2x10^14 Pa, roughly two thousand times diamond's compressive strength, which no material can survive. So the stated number is simultaneously correct and unusable: it cannot distinguish an avalanche from a lance, and the two differ by a factor of about a million in the quantity that decides whether the shell breaks. The page's own counter line, 'enough raw kinetic weight can fracture it outright', names the wrong variable for the same reason: weight is not what does it, concentration is.

options.option: Restate the ward's capacity as a stress - a figure in megapascals or gigapascals - and let an attack's footprint decide whether it gets through.
options.changes: Makes the ward checkable against any attack a player can describe and turns the counter into a real tactical choice (spread or concentrate); requires every comparable ward page to be restated the same way, and Part Eleven ladders Strike Force in newtons, so a conversion convention would be needed.

options.option: Keep the force figure and add a stated minimum footprint below which the ward does not resist at all.
options.changes: Smallest edit that fixes the failure mode; introduces a threshold number the system does not currently supply for any ward.

options.option: Rule that a ward distributes any incoming load across its whole surface by construction, so force is the right unit for it.
options.changes: Legitimises the page as written and makes wards enormously strong against concentrated attacks, which removes the piercing and shot routes from the counterplay register for every warded target.

options.option: Add Durability rather than Strike Force as the ward's rating facet, and ladder it separately.
options.changes: Uses the facet Part Eleven already defines for exactly this ('capacity to absorb, deflect or endure incoming energy without structural failure') and needs that facet laddered against Grade, which the corpus does not currently do.

quote_a: - **Physics Domain** · Electromagnetism || - **Wellspring** · Judicium (primary); Sublimatio (secondary)
quote_b: ### Sublimatio · *The Ascending Breath* — **Analogue** · Sublimation. Solid to vapour with no liquid phase, below the triple point. ... **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Ardency Compression, Tempering Clarity. ... [and the entry immediately following] ### Sublimare · *The Rising Breath* — **Analogue** · Fractional distillation. Separation by differential volatility. ... Where Sublimatio skips a phase, Sublimare separates a mixture.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md
why: Two errors about the same current, and the second is more interesting than the first. (1) The page files both its Wellsprings under 'Family - Fulguria'. Judicium is Fulguria. Sublimatio is in the Vectoria register, Physics Domain Mechanics, and the page's own Physics Domain line gives only 'Electromagnetism', so the second current has no domain on the page at all. (2) The page assigns Sublimatio a separating function: it 'supplies the refining step that separates what passes cleanly from what is arrested, purified or annihilated, in the same way a sublimation vessel separates a purified vapor from the residue that never rises'. Sublimatio's register describes a practitioner skipping a phase, with residue as a by-product rather than a product, and the register then draws the exact distinction the page needs, in the entry immediately after: 'Where Sublimatio skips a phase, Sublimare separates a mixture.' The function the page describes is Sublimare's by the register's own contrastive sentence. Separately, neither declared current supplies any of the page's three governing Sub-Stats: Judicium strengthens Gnosis Acuity, Analysis and Diagnosis; Sublimatio strengthens Ardency Compression and Tempering Clarity; the FOW line governs on Ardency Density and Resilience Integrity and Anchoring.

options.option: Correct the Family and Physics Domain lines, and swap Sublimatio for Sublimare as the secondary.
options.changes: Two small edits that make the page's own mechanism sentence true; costs the page Sublimatio's Failure line ('Residue accumulation'), which is the best unwritten cost it currently has access to.

options.option: Correct the Family line and keep Sublimatio, restating its contribution as phase-skipping rather than separation.
options.changes: Keeps the current and its Failure; requires rewriting the Mechanism clause, since phase-skipping does not by itself sort arrivals and the sorting has to come from Judicium alone.

options.option: Carry both Sublimatio and Sublimare, one for the clean crossing and one for the separation.
options.changes: Most faithful to what the page describes; raises the harmonisation count to three across two Families and brings two Failure lines onto the page.

options.option: Rule that Wellsprings adjacent in a register may be read interchangeably where a page's described function fits either.
options.changes: Would close a class of rows quickly and would erase the register's own contrastive sentences, which are written precisely to keep neighbouring currents distinct.

quote_a: - **Governing Primary** · Ardency (Density), secondary Resilience (Integrity, Anchoring)
quote_b: **Ward** — Defence against law-breaking, reality-overwriting and Domain-erasure forces, including techniques aimed at collapsing, inverting or redirecting the character's own Domain. What stands between a character and an effect that says they do not exist. || **Oath** — Structural durability of active vows, contracts and Fate-anchor oaths under attempts to sever, invert or weaponise them.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md, Resilience
why: The page governs on 'Ardency (Density), secondary Resilience (Integrity, Anchoring)'. Ardency Density is defensible and Part Twelve nearly says so in the page's own words - 'Structural weight and coherence of anything a working leaves standing ... Whether your ward outlasts the siege'. But two Resilience Sub-Stats describe this working more exactly than anything on the page, and neither is named. Ward is 'Defence against law-breaking, reality-overwriting and Domain-erasure forces ... What stands between a character and an effect that says they do not exist', which is what a bastion is for and what the page's own Target Response describes it doing. Oath is 'Structural durability of active vows, contracts and Fate-anchor oaths under attempts to sever, invert or weaponise them', which is the page's stated self-destruct condition read from the defending side: 'the barrier's own judgment logic makes it fail instantly if Opalis's stated intent and her actual intent diverge while it stands'. That condition is the most exploitable thing on the page - the Counterplay register's entry on the vow says an opponent who knows the terms 'holds a weapon that does not require touching him' - and the Sub-Stat that would defend it is absent. Note the gates: Ward requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C, which the page does not declare; Oath requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B, which is exactly the page's declared Path and would pass. The page derived its Sub-Stats from what a barrier is made of and never asked what this barrier is for.

options.option: Add Resilience Ward and Resilience Oath to the FOW line.
options.changes: Makes the working's Sub-Stats describe the working; Ward's gate then requires Spirit Path, which the page does not declare, so the Path line would have to move as well (see SA-NUM-BASTION-PATHGATE).

options.option: Add Oath only, since its gate passes on the declared Attraction Path, and leave Ward out.
options.changes: One clean addition with no Path consequence, and it directly prices the working's most exploitable feature; leaves the barrier's primary defensive function ungoverned.

options.option: Keep the FOW line and state on the page that the intent-divergence condition is not defended by any Sub-Stat, deliberately.
options.changes: Makes the vulnerability a design choice rather than an oversight and is strongly in the working's favour narratively; means no amount of investment can ever harden it, which is unusual in the system.

options.option: Rule that a working's governing Sub-Stats are derived from its Wellsprings rather than from its function, and accept the mismatch generally.
options.changes: Would settle a recurring class of rows in this batch in one move and would make most technique pages' FOW lines predictable from their Wellspring lines; it would also mean no working is governed by the Sub-Stat named for it unless a Wellspring happens to strengthen that one.

quote_a: - **Path gate** · Attraction Path
quote_b: **Density** requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, with inscription and glyph-chain durability requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Seven, Ardency Gates
why: The page declares Path gate Attraction Path and Grade required A-Grade, and governs primarily on Ardency Density. Part Seven: 'Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B.' A-Grade exceeds B, so the Body gate binds and the page declares no Body at all. The secondary Sub-Stats are better but not clean. Resilience Integrity is 'open, though the conversion of prior fractures into reinforcement requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed B' - the page claims no such conversion, so it passes. Resilience Anchoring is 'open, though resistance to memory erasure and false implantation requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C' - and the page lists memory-based illusions as one of its two weaknesses, so the clause that would answer its own stated weakness is priced on a Path it does not declare either. The same failure on Ardency Density is already logged for another Opalis page (SA-NUM-OBELISK-PATHGATE), which makes this a question about a practitioner rather than about one technique, and Opalis has no character card to settle it (SA-GAP-OPALIS-NO-CARD).

options.option: Add Body Path to the page's Path gate alongside Attraction.
options.changes: Clears Ardency Density here and on the Obelisk page; leaves the Anchoring memory clause still on Spirit, and commits a practitioner with no card to two Paths on the evidence of two technique pages.

options.option: Replace Ardency Density with a Sub-Stat whose gate the declared Path clears - Resilience Oath is Attraction at Stage IV and would pass.
options.changes: Keeps the Path line and changes what the working is governed by; Part Twelve's Density entry names wards explicitly, so the page would be giving up the Sub-Stat written for its object.

options.option: Write Opalis a character card and settle her Paths there once for all four of her pages.
options.changes: Closes SA-GAP-OPALIS-NO-CARD and both Path rows and several derived-eta questions at the same time; a real writing job and the only option that fixes the underlying cause rather than an instance.

options.option: Rule that the Path gate on a page is a statement about the technique's routing and not about the practitioner's commitment.
options.changes: Would separate two things the system currently conflates and close many rows across the batch; requires Part Seven to say which of the two it is gating, since it currently reads as the practitioner's.

quote_a: **Cost** · An estimated 5,000 EU while the ward stands, chosen conservatively for a Stage VI standing working, plus the tremor through Opalis's own Soul Crystal the card describes when the barrier is made to arrest something large.
quote_b: **EU · Essence Units** — the raw reserve. "Scales with Temperance Stage, governed primarily by Tempering Yield." No formula converts a Stage into an EU figure anywhere in the system.
path_b: imports/system-accounts/_method.md, section III, citing wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The page gives a resource cost of 'an estimated 5,000 EU while the ward stands, chosen conservatively for a Stage VI standing working', and its duration as 'an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives duration only in the old system's turns'. Both are explicitly flagged by the page as estimates rather than derivations, which is honest and is also precisely what the batch may not carry forward: no formula anywhere in the system converts a Stage into an EU figure, so 5,000 is not conservative or unconservative, it is unanchored.
