The duration has two separate problems on top of that - no turn length is fixed anywhere in the corpus (SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH), and 'Law Two' is cited on this page and three others as the authority for the only numbers they give and is defined nowhere in the corpus (SA-UNATT-LAW-TWO). The practical consequence is that the one cost this working states and the one duration it states both rest on nothing, on a page whose other numbers - radius, peak force, Grade - are quoted correctly from Part Eleven and Part Four.

options.option: Replace the figure with null and state the cost qualitatively until an EU formula exists.
options.changes: Consistent with the rest of the batch and with the page's own honesty; leaves the working with no quantified resource cost, so the fairness test rests entirely on the intent-divergence condition.

options.option: Publish an EU-by-Stage table, even a coarse one, and derive the figure from it.
options.changes: Closes SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA across the whole corpus and is the single highest-value missing table in this batch; every page that has estimated an EU cost would then have to be rechecked against it.

options.option: Price standing workings as a rate (EU per second) rather than a total, and state the rate.
options.changes: Correct for a working that is explicitly 'held open rather than fired' and makes duration and cost one decision instead of two; still needs an anchor for the rate.

options.option: Define Law Two, wherever it belongs, so the four pages citing it have an authority to cite.
options.changes: Closes SA-UNATT-LAW-TWO and whatever it settles here; does not by itself anchor the EU number, since Law Two is invoked on this page for the duration rather than the cost.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Incoming force below the S-Grade energy-yield ceiling (up to roughly 24.3 terajoules, per the Strike Force benchmarks for that Grade) is absorbed as a glancing structural event rather than a wound; force above that ceiling still gets through, since the hardening raises the failure threshold and does not remove one.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four; and III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md, S row
why: The citation is correct and the consequence is not. Part Eleven's S-Grade ceiling is 2.42672x10^13 J, which the page quotes accurately as roughly 24.3 terajoules, and then asks a human body to receive it 'as a glancing structural event rather than a wound'. 24.3 TJ is 5,808 tonnes of TNT, 5.8 kilotons. Vaporising the practitioner outright costs about 2.5x10^8 J - heating 100 kg of water-like tissue from 310 K to 373 K is 2.6x10^7 J and the latent heat of vaporisation is 2.26x10^8 J - so the stated ceiling is about ninety-seven thousand times the energy needed to boil him away entirely. Taken as heat at a specific heat of 3,500 J/(kg K) it is a temperature rise of 6.9x10^7 K, the interior of a star. Taken as momentum, sqrt(2E/m) for 100 kg gives 6.97x10^5 m/s: Mach 2,030, or 0.23 percent of light speed. Note what is not wrong here: the page's framing is honest ('the hardening raises the failure threshold and does not remove one'), the Grade citation is exact, and the qualitative claim - that blunt force below some threshold becomes a structural event rather than a wound - is sound material physics. What fails is the location of the threshold, which the page inherits from Part Eleven's Grade band rather than choosing. This is the same failure as SA-PHYS-REPRISAL-YIELD-VS-STAGGER on the same practitioner, and it recurs wherever a page takes a Grade band's energy figure and describes a person surviving it.

options.option: State the absorption ceiling as a stress or a force rather than an energy, since a body fails at a stress: a figure in the hundreds of megapascals distributed is defensible, and an energy is not.
options.changes: Makes the working checkable against any described blow and brings it into line with what the material table actually supports; requires a convention for converting Part Eleven's joule bands into stresses, which the corpus does not have.

options.option: Lower the stated ceiling to what a stone-curve body can plausibly take and accept that it does not cover the top of S-Grade.
options.changes: Honest and costs the working its headline claim; the working becomes a defence against everything up to a point rather than against a Grade, which is arguably what a failure threshold is.

options.option: Rule generally that Part Eleven's energy bands are notional scale markers rather than joule figures to be conserved against.
options.changes: Would close a large class of rows across this batch at once - the Obelisk, the Lance, the Reprisal and this page all fail the same way - and would remove the corpus's only quantitative link between Grade and real force, which is the thing that makes any of these checks possible.

options.option: Keep the figure and state where the energy goes, naming a sink.
options.changes: Preserves the claim and requires the page to answer the question it currently skips; at 24.3 TJ no sink that leaves the practitioner in the scene is available, so this option is stated mainly so the ruling can say so.

quote_a: **Weakness** · Entropy fields and dissolution-type magics unmake the coagulated coherence directly rather than testing its failure threshold, which routes around the technique's entire premise; Sublimatio-adjacent workings that convert matter to a higher state without an intermediate stage are named on the card as a specific hazard for the same reason.
quote_b: **Effect** · Drakvor's own flesh stops behaving like flesh. Skin, bone, and the Essence running under both take on the failure curve of stone rather than the failure curve of a body, and blows that would open him instead ring off him.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/The Last Monolith.md:17
why: The Mechanism and Effect agree that the body takes on 'the failure curve of stone rather than the failure curve of a body'. That is a real and specific constitutive change, and it has a direction. Cortical bone runs roughly 170-200 MPa in compression and 120-150 MPa in tension, with a fracture toughness around 2-12 MPa*m^0.5 and a strain to failure of 1-3 percent. Granite runs roughly 130-250 MPa in compression - an even trade - and 7-25 MPa in tension, with a toughness of 0.5-2 MPa*m^0.5 and a strain to failure of 0.1-0.3 percent. So the exchange is: compression, no change; tension, about ten times weaker; toughness, about five times lower; strain to failure, about ten to twenty times lower. And a brittle solid has no plastic reserve, so it does not bruise or deform, it cracks, and a crack runs at 0.4-0.6 of the shear wave speed, 1,200-1,800 m/s in rock, which is faster than any reaction. The page's stated Weakness line names only entropy fields, dissolution magics and Sublimatio-adjacent workings. Every one of those is exotic. The weakness the stated mechanism actually produces is available to anyone holding a spear, a pick, a hook or a lever, because a thrust that wedges, a pull, a twist and a joint lock are all tension or shear. The register two files away states the principle without being asked: 'Masonry is enormously strong in compression and nearly worthless in tension, which is why the arch exists' (Petralon, Vectoria). The Effect line's 'blows that would open him instead ring off him' is correct and is a statement about crushing only.

options.option: Add tensile and shear loading to the Weakness line: thrusts, levers, joint locks and hooked weapons, with the material reason stated.
options.changes: Gives the working a counter an ordinary soldier can use and makes the state a real trade rather than a strict upgrade; substantially lowers the technique's power against mundane opposition, which is where it currently has none.

options.option: Narrow the Effect line so the hardening is explicitly compressive-only and says so.
options.changes: Same outcome by the other door and keeps the Weakness line short; makes the working read as armour rather than as transformation, which may be the more accurate description of it.

options.option: Add a second current whose register supplies tensile toughness, so the state is not purely brittle.
options.changes: Keeps the working strong and requires naming a current the page does not carry; the Materia register's options each bring their own Failure line, and the harmonisation count is already flagged on the card.

options.option: Rule that a Coagula hardening is isotropic in the system's terms and that the real-material tension asymmetry does not carry over.
options.changes: Closes the row by declaring the physical account out of scope for this working; conflicts with the standard the batch is written to, since the page's own Mechanism is stated in materials language and invites the comparison.

quote_a: **Wellspring** · Coagula (primary) · Judicium (secondary)
quote_b: **Monolithion**, the Enduring Monument. Strengthens Vitality Tolerance, Resilience Persistence, Dominion Gravity. Presence becomes geological.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md, Part Thirteen, Materia
why: The technique is called The Last Monolith. The Materia register contains a Wellspring called Monolithion, the Enduring Monument, whose entire gloss is 'Presence becomes geological' and which strengthens Vitality Tolerance, Resilience Persistence and Dominion Gravity - which is what a sustained held state costs and what it is for. The page declares Coagula and Judicium and not Monolithion. This is not automatically an error: the page's two declared currents supply its four governing Sub-Stats exactly and clear every Path gate, which makes this the best-derived FOW line in the batch, and adding a third current would raise a harmonisation count the practitioner's own card already flags ('Six Wellsprings claimed woven into it... Fifty-four of the Sixty remain untouched'). But the omission is conspicuous enough to need a ruling rather than a shrug, because the page's stated duration limit and its release cost are both endurance questions and neither declared current addresses endurance at all. why: The page has Judicium 'reading the geometry and force of an incoming blow closely enough that the hardening can present its density exactly where the blow will land rather than uniformly and too late'. That is a reactive defence, and a reactive defence has a latency floor. A mechanical redistribution inside a hardened body propagates at the speed of sound in that body; longitudinal wave speed in granite is about 5,500 m/s, so across a 2 m body the news takes 2/5500 = 0.36 ms. Part Four puts S-Grade travel speed at Mach 25 to 200, which is 8,575 to 68,600 m/s, and in 0.36 ms such an attack covers 3.1 m to 25 m. So the Judicium read must precede contact by at least the body's own acoustic transit time, which sets a minimum detection standoff of roughly 3 m at the bottom of S-Grade and roughly 25 m at the top - against a Part Eleven S-Grade Contact Range of 5-15 m. The requirement brackets the engagement distance, which means the working is viable at the low end of its own Grade and not at the high end. The gap is that nothing in the system ladders how far a Gnosis read reaches, or how early. Part Eleven ladders Projected Force Range but defines Range as 'the spatial envelope across which force remains coherent', which is not a sensing distance (see SA-GAP-RANGE-LADDER), and Part Twelve's Gnosis entries describe what a read resolves rather than at what distance. Without that ladder, every reactive defence in the corpus is unpriceable in the one variable that decides whether it works.

options.changes: Removes the latency floor and requires the system to say how fast a working's own internal state propagates, which it currently says nowhere; that number would govern every reactive defence.
